#### RF-128 — A handle shows the browser's focus indicator, and not Material's

Tier A, **closed on 2026-11-25** (the last note), pre-existing. Before closure: open. Until the architect's note of 2026-11-24 it was Tier C. Registered on 2026-11-24 by the architect, on `repo/sortable-observations-1`, on the owner's third observation of that day, relayed by the coordinator: _"ещё один: при фокусе на ручке outline синий. Я так понимаю, нативный, и не знаю, нам надо это трогать, или нет"_ ("One more: when the handle has focus, its outline is blue. As I understand it, it's native, and I don't know whether we should touch it"). Read at `114270083` in Chromium, Firefox and WebKit ([readings](sortable-observations-1/checks/focus-indicator.txt) and [the candidate's](sortable-observations-1/checks/handle-indicator.txt), [probe](sortable-observations-1/probes/handle-indicator.mjs)).

- **Whose element:** the consumer's, in the item's `lead` or `trail` slot. In a sortable list the package makes it a button: `sortItem` writes its `tabindex`, `role="button"`, name, description and `touch-action`.
- **What draws it:** the browser. Nothing in the package or the story has a rule for it, and the computed outline is `auto`, 1px in Chromium and Firefox and 3px in WebKit, in the engine's color. That is the same for `mx-icon`, a `span` and a native `button`. A `mx-icon-button` as a handle already draws Material's, on its inner button.
- **What says what it should be:** `RD-31` property 4 makes the handle focusable and names it, and is silent on its indicator. Material has no handle in its list pages. Every control of the package draws the system's focus indicator: 3px, `md.sys.color.secondary`, 2px outside.
- **Why it matters, and how little:** focus is visible today, so nothing is inaccessible. A button that the package makes looks unlike every other control, and like three things in the three engines.
- **Required property:** a focused handle that the list made a button shows Material's focus indicator, and a page's own rule on it still wins.
- **Candidate read:** `::slotted([data-handle]:focus-visible)` in the item's sheet. In the three engines, on static and button items, it draws the indicator on `mx-icon`, `span` and `button`, a page rule on the handle wins over it, and `* { outline: 0 }` removes it, as it removes the browser's. `mx-icon-button` is unchanged, with one indicator. An `!important` outline isn't taken: the handle is the consumer's element.
- **Answered by the owner on 2026-11-24,** in chat, relayed by the coordinator: **(a)**. _"3) (a)"_.
- **The question as asked, Q1 — who owns the handle's indicator?**
  - **(a) The package draws it, by that rule. Recommended. Chosen:** the package makes the handle a button, so the button looks like its buttons, whatever the consumer used. It costs one rule in each item's sheet, not measured, also for a plain `mx-list`, and a focusable `[data-handle]` that a consumer puts there takes it.
  - (b) The documentation says that the handle keeps the browser's indicator, and how to style it: `mx-sortable-list [data-handle]:focus-visible { outline: … }` works today (read). It costs nothing, and each consumer does it or doesn't.
  - (c) The story styles its own handle only, so the Storybook looks right and a consumer's doesn't.
  - (d) Nothing changes.
- **Rows,** `spec`, in each engine: the outline of a focused handle in each slot and each kind of item against `focusTokens`, and a page's rule winning. **Witness:** the outline row fails before the repair.
- **Not read:** an `mx-icon-button` handle's accessible nodes, where the host also has `role="button"`.
- **Plan needed:** no. **Ready** for an implementer. The rule is adopted in the items' sheets, and takes the values of the shared `focusTokens`, 2px outside. `RF-125` gives the item's own variables the list's −3px, and both are on the item's `:host`, so the handle's offset needs a variable of its own. The two can land in either order.
- **Size:** _small_.

**Dated 2026-11-24 by the implementer, on `material-x/handle-focus-1`: not implemented, and returned to the architect.** Requested by the coordinator. The code disagrees with the entry in the `trail` slot. Read on the built elements in Playwright's Chromium 158, Firefox 159 and WebKit 27.2, with the entry's rule as a source change that is restored ([patch](handle-focus-1/checks/handle-focus-scratch.patch.txt)) and as adopted sheets ([reading](handle-focus-1/checks/handle-paint.txt), [probe](handle-focus-1/probes/handle-paint.mjs)), for the four kinds of handle, two kinds of item, two slots, and LTR and RTL. A handle's own pixels below are those in the indicator's color. The whole item also changes by 200 to 202 pixels when focus enters it, whatever the handle is, and their cause wasn't read.

- **The `.trail` slot has `overflow: hidden`, and it fits the handle, so it clips what lies outside the handle.** With the rule, a trailing `mx-icon`, `span` or `button` has the right computed outline and shows 0 pixels of it, in each engine, item and direction. In the `lead` slot it is whole: 324 pixels for a 20px `mx-icon`, which is the ring's area.
- **So the rule alone makes a trailing handle worse.** It replaces the browser's outline, of which some is visible today. Beyond the item's own change, LTR, `main` shows about 88 pixels for `mx-icon`, 164 for `span` and 228 for `button` in Chromium, and about 12, 54 and 240 in WebKit. In Firefox it shows 0 for `mx-icon`, 21 for `span` and 118 for `button`. The entry's _"focus is visible today"_ is false for a trailing `mx-icon` in Firefox. With the rule none of these shows anything.
- **A trailing `mx-icon-button` is clipped today too:** 92 to 93 of its 317 to 324 pixels show in Chromium and WebKit, and 0 in Firefox.
- **The entry's candidate reading** was of computed styles, which clipping doesn't change. It holds as far as it goes.
- **Candidates, read for the paint alone:**
  - `.trail { overflow: visible }`: whole in both slots, in the three engines, and for `mx-icon-button`. It costs the clipping of trailing text that is wider than the slot, which wasn't read. The slot is `flex: 0 0 min-content`.
  - `overflow: clip` with `overflow-clip-margin: 5px`: whole in Chromium and Firefox, nothing in WebKit.
  - An offset of −3px in `.trail`: whole and inside the handle, in the three engines, so an indicator over the handle's content. `mx-icon-button` stays clipped.
  - A padding of 5px with a margin of −5px, under `:has-slotted`: whole on button items in Firefox alone. In Chromium and WebKit the sheet changed nothing there. The cause wasn't read, and this isn't evidence against the form.
- **What the rule needs otherwise holds:** the list's own thickness and color equal `focusTokens`' (3px, `md.sys.color.secondary`), so only the offset needs a variable, `--_handle-focus-indicator-outline-offset`.
- **Not read:** Safari, sizes, rows, and the list's long trailing text.

**Dated 2026-11-24 by the architect, on the implementer's return, relayed by the coordinator. The owner's (a) stands. The trail slot's clip goes, as `RF-135`, in the same unit. Ready again for an implementer,** on `material-x/handle-focus-1` with `main` at `751b1fb81` merged. Read on the built elements in Playwright's Chromium 158, Firefox 159 and WebKit 27.2.

- **The return is right, and so is its reading.** The entry's candidate read computed styles only. (a) needs the indicator to be seen, and in `trail` it isn't while the slot clips.
- **What the clip protects: nothing that was found** ([reading](handle-focus-1/checks/trail-clip.txt), [probe](handle-focus-1/probes/trail-clip.mjs), 19 contents, two kinds of item, two directions, three engines). Between `hidden` and `visible` no box moves, and no size differs. **Long trailing text isn't clipped today:** the slot is `flex: 0 0 min-content` and the text is `nowrap`, so in a 300px item the slot is 538 to 581px wide and the text runs out of the item in either case, with no ellipsis. Short and wrapped text, icons, buttons, a checkbox, and 56px and 150px boxes are drawn the same, but for at most 5 pixels of a glyph's edge in wrapped text. What the clip does cut:
  - what a page lets overflow a child that it bounded itself, such as `display: block; max-inline-size: 80px` (480 to 750 pixels). With its own `overflow: hidden; text-overflow: ellipsis`, which is the form that gives an ellipsis, it reads the same in both;
  - a shadow (an elevated `mx-button`, 105 to 130 pixels, and any page's own), a negative margin, and focus indicators (`RF-135`).
- **Where it came from:** `3632ccd77` wrote the clip and the ellipsis for the **slotted texts** of `.label`, `.overline`, `.support` and `.trail`, and `663e921c7` moved it to the slots. `md.comp.list` has color, font, size, weight, tracking and line height for the trailing text, and nothing of overflow. Material's pages weren't read.
- **Tier.** It was C, for _"focus is visible today, so nothing is inaccessible"_. That sentence is false for a trailing `mx-icon` in Firefox, and by the vocabulary of [review-findings.md](../.agents/docs/review-findings.md#tier) a page sees another rendering, so it is A. The invisible focus itself is **a finding of its own, `RF-135`,** because it isn't the handle's: a `mx-icon-button` in a plain list has it too.
- **Not taken, for `trail`:** `overflow: clip` with a margin (WebKit paints nothing); an offset of −3px (the indicator lies on the handle's content, and it leaves `mx-icon-button` clipped, so `RF-135` needs another repair anyway); padding with a negative margin (it reads whole in one engine and one kind of item, and keeps a clip that protects nothing); `overflow: visible` only while a handle has focus (the slot would change its overflow with focus, for no gain); and (b), (c) or (d) for trailing handles only, which makes the same handle look different by slot.
- **Nothing is the owner's to answer.** (a) is his answer, and what the repair removes has no use that was found. **Told to him, as a cost:** a page that lets its own bounded trailing child overflow sees it spill.

#### RF-129 — The sortable list takes the baseline `dragged` tokens, and Material's `reorder` set is the one for its lists

Tier A, **closed on 2026-11-25** (the last note), pre-existing. Before closure: open. Registered on 2026-11-24 by the architect, on `drag/command-signal-1`, from the note _"Seen, and not registered"_ of `RF-127`, on the owner's answer in chat, relayed by the coordinator: _"Точно да 👍"_ ("Definitely yes"). `RF-128` is the highest `RF-` on any branch on `origin`, so this is the next free number. Read at `73a2320ef` on the built elements in Chromium, Firefox and WebKit ([readings](command-signal-1/checks/reorder-colors.txt), [probe](command-signal-1/probes/reorder-colors.mjs)).

- **What happens:** the drop zone is `list-item.dragged.state-layer`'s color and opacity. The lifted item takes `list-item.dragged`'s shape, label color and elevation, with its resting container. The store's display group for these is _"Dragged (baseline only)"_, whose description says: _"The dragged state of baseline lists. Use "reorder" tokens for the dragged state of expressive lists."_ The package's lists are expressive: they take `container.expressive.shape` and `segmented.gap`. Of the reorder set they take the shadow's color alone (`RF-77`).
- **The set, `md.comp.list.reorder`,** described as _"For reordering a list item using a drag handle or accessible alternative. Only use for Expressive lists."_ It has twelve tokens, none deprecated:

  | Token | Value | Part, and what it is today |
  | --- | --- | --- |
  | `drop-zone.color` | `surface-container-low` | The placeholder. Today `on-surface` at 0.16 |
  | `container.color` | `tertiary-container` | The lifted item's container. Today `surface`, or `secondary-container` when selected |
  | `shape` | `corner.large`, 16 px | The lifted item's corners. Today `list-item.dragged`'s, the same 16 px |
  | `shadow-color` | `shadow` | Its shadow. Already adopted |
  | `label-text.color` | `on-tertiary-container` | Today `on-surface` |
  | `overline.color`, `supporting-text.color`, `trailing-supporting-text.color` | `on-tertiary-container` | Today `on-surface-variant` |
  | `leading-icon.color`, `trailing-icon.color` | `on-tertiary-container` | Today `on-surface-variant`, and `on-surface` for an interactive item's trailing icon. A handle with `mx-icon` is one of these |
  | `state-layer.color`, `state-layer.opacity` | `on-tertiary-container`, 0.1 | The ripple of the held press, on an interactive item. Today `on-surface` at 0.1 |

- **What the set doesn't have:** an elevation, and a shape or an opacity of the drop zone. `list-item.dragged.container.elevation`, level 4, is the only elevation Material names for a dragged list item, and the set's shadow color has a meaning only with one. **Compose Material3 does the same** (androidx `0c24a09f8`, read by the architect): `ListItemDefaults.kt` takes the container, the content and the shape from `ReorderListTokens`, and `draggedElevation` from `ListTokens.ItemDraggedContainerElevation`. Its order for the container is disabled, dragged, selected, and it animates the colors. Its `ItemDropZoneColor` isn't used in those two files. Material's own list pages don't describe a reorder, as `RF-127` read them.
- **Why it is a problem:** the list shows the state of another kind of list, against the token set's own text.
- **Required properties:**
  1. **In a pointer drag,** from `onStart` to `onEnd`, the lifted item's container, shape, text, icons and press ripple take the reorder tokens, for a static, a button and a link item, with a handle or without. They take precedence over selected, hovered, focused and pressed. A disabled item keeps its disabled look: a handle lifts a disabled button item, in the three engines.
  2. **The container's color and the text's change together.** A static item's host is its container and drag's lift freezes the host's color and background inline, so the item needs its own over them. Read: without that, the static item's background stays at rest while its label takes the new color.
  3. **The drop zone** is `reorder.list-item.drop-zone.color`, opaque. Its shape stays the list's.
  4. **The elevation stays** `list-item.dragged.container.elevation`, over `--_drag-duration`, for both kinds of operation. No other `list-item.dragged` token is rendered.
  5. **A key move** shows no reorder color and no drop zone (Q1). The lifted item keeps its resting colors, and its corners and press ripple take no `reorder` and no `list-item.dragged` token. Its elevation rises as today.
  6. **Consumer overrides:** `--md-list-item-container-color` and `--md-list-item-container-shape` win on a lifted item, as at rest, and `--md-list-container-shape` on the drop zone. **A page's own `background-color` or `color` on an `mx-list-item` host holds at rest and in a key move, and not in a pointer drag.** Today it holds there too, so `RF-68` property 6 and a row of `list-roles` change. Its rect, padding, border and overflow still hold, with a page's rule on `[popover]` too.
  7. **Only `list/sortable-list` carries the reorder item tokens** (`CONTRIBUTING.md` §7, in `RD-31`'s direction). A plain list never drags.
- **Candidate read, and recommended:** the list's own sheet sets the item's private properties on `::slotted(:state(drag))`. In the three engines it reaches a static, a button and a selected button item while it is hovered, focused and pressed, because the list's tree outranks the item's own `:host` rules, so no order of states has to change. The same values on `:host(:state(drag))` in the items' main sheet lose on a selected item, and on a button item's trailing icon. For a static item, a rule of the list's sheet on its lifted host, by its tag name, sets its background color and color with `!important`. An important rule of the list's tree outranks the inline value that drag's lift writes, and the page's rules. It applies to static items alone, because an interactive item's host has no container of its own. **All of it is in the list's sheet, under the list's state from `RF-127`,** so it doesn't apply in a key move, the item gets no second state, and the item's sheets don't change for it. The rule for the private properties needs `:not(:state(disabled))` for property 1. Read on 2026-11-24 in the three engines, with a page's rules, a consumer's `--md-list-item-container-color` and a disabled item ([readings](command-signal-1/checks/reorder-list-sheet.txt), the same probe). It replaces the first candidate, a rule on `:host(:popover-open)` in the static item's sheet, which would need a second state on the item. The sheet is one that only `list/sortable-list` adopts (property 7), because `mx-list` adopts the default one too.
- **What differs to see:**
  - The lifted item is filled, `tertiary-container`, where today only its shadow and corners say that it is lifted. Its color changes at once, at the grab and at the drop. The 650 ms flight after the drop is in the resting colors, with the shadow falling as today.
  - The drop zone is **much fainter.** In the default theme its contrast with `surface` is 1.05 in light and 1.08 in dark, and today's is 1.39 and 1.49. On a page whose background is `surface-container-low` it can't be seen. The lifted item is far stronger, 4.39 and 5.82 against `surface`.
  - The text on the lifted item has a contrast of 4.53 and 4.63 in that theme.
- **Why a key move is separate from RF-127's footprint:** with the reorder color set at `onStart` for every operation, a key move whose commit comes in the next task paints it for 1 or 2 frames, and one after 100 ms for 2 to 6 ([readings](command-signal-1/checks/reorder-colors.txt)). Without it, 0. So this unit needs `drag:DRD-71`.
- **Answered by the owner on 2026-11-24:** (a) to all three, in chat, relayed by the coordinator: _"Q1-Q4: (a)"_. Its first letter is `drag:DRD-71`'s.
- **Q1, for the owner — does a key move take the reorder colors?**
  - **(a) No. Recommended. Chosen:** it would flash a filled item for a frame, as the footprint did. The set's _"accessible alternative"_ is best read as an alternative that has a progress, such as grab mode, which would take the look.
  - (b) Yes, with the flash, or with a transition of the colors that hides most of it and needs Q2 (b).
- **Q2, for the owner — do the colors change at once, or over time?**
  - **(a) At once. Recommended for this unit. Chosen:** every other state of the package's items changes its colors at once.
  - (b) Over time, as Compose does. It is a unit of its own: the colors are on five parts and on the consumer's slotted icons, the lift freezes the host's transitions, and it isn't read.
- **Q3, for the owner — is the fainter drop zone accepted?**
  - **(a) Yes, the token as Material gives it. Recommended,** on his answer. **Chosen.** The moving items and the lifted item also show where it lands.
  - (b) Keep today's drop zone and take the rest. It mixes the two sets.
- **`RD-31`** property 4 is amended, in its [eighth amendment](decisions/RD-31.md), with the recommended answers, which are the owner's.

- **Rows,** `spec`, in each engine: the lifted item's container, label and icons against the reorder tokens, resolved through the bridge, for a static, a button and a selected button item, held at the press and after a hover, and back at rest after the drop. A static item with `--md-list-item-container-color`. The drop zone against `drop-zone.color`, with opacity 1 (it replaces _"should give the placeholder the list footprint color"_). A disabled button item lifted by its handle keeps its disabled look. `browser`: in a key move the lifted item has its resting colors and corners in the `reorder` handler, and in each frame while a commit after 100 ms is pending. A row that counts the frames of a commit in the next task proves nothing: with the reorder look in a key move it read 0 frames in a run of WebKit. A static item's `background-color` set by a page holds at rest, in a key move, and after the drop. `list-roles`' lift row keeps rect, padding and overflow, and gets the new color expectation for a pointer drag. **Witness:** the token rows fail before the change, and the key row fails with the colors set for both kinds. Drag-state baselines, if any, are the owner's to record.

#### RF-130 — A control loses the component's own `aria-*` when the host's same attribute is removed

Tier A, **closed on 2026-11-25** (the last note), pre-existing. Before closure: open. Registered on 2026-11-24 by the architect, on `core/use-aria-1`, from `RF-124`'s ruling. `RF-129` is the highest `RF-` on any branch on `origin` (`drag/command-signal-1`), so this is the next free number. Read at `114270083` and at `20997b0e2` in Chromium, Firefox and WebKit, with the same result ([readings](aria-removed-1/checks/ruling.txt)).

- **What happens:** a component writes its own value of an `aria-*` on its control, from its own source, and the host has the same name. When the page removes the host's attribute, `useARIA` removes the control's. The component's source hasn't changed, so it doesn't write its value again. The state stays, and the control doesn't say it. The same happens when the source and the host's attribute change in one task, because the mirror runs after. Read for `aria-disabled` (a link with `disabled`), `aria-current` (`mx-list-link-item` with `selected`), `aria-selected` (`mx-list-button-item`), `aria-checked` (`mx-switch-button`), and `aria-invalid` and `aria-required` (the text field).
- **The reverse,** by reading: while the host has the name, the last of the two to change is on the control, and a connect gives the host's. So a disabled link whose host says `aria-disabled="false"` says it too.
- **Why it is a problem:** the page doesn't have to misuse anything to meet it. A link's `aria-disabled` and `aria-current` are the page's to give, and it can change to `disabled` or `selected`. The validation names are less likely, because the JSDoc asks for `error` and `required`.
- **Required property:** while the host doesn't give a name, the control shows the component's own value of it, whatever the order in which the two changed. What it shows while the host gives it is the plan's to say.
- **Not established:** how the component's value reaches the mirror. The text fields do it for two names, in the transformer's answer for `null`. `useDisableableLinkable` reads the host's value when `disabled` goes, and nothing does the other direction.
- **Order:** after `RF-124`. `RF-94`'s plan may replace the mirror, and answers this one with it or leaves it.
- **Plan needed:** yes, by the architect.
- **Size:** _medium_.

**Added 2026-11-24 by the architect, for the plan,** from `RF-124`'s [recheck](reviews/aria-removed-1/feature-proof-recheck-claude.md), read in the three engines at `80c5db113`:

- **Before the first connect.** A name that the host gets and loses in one task, before it is first connected, removes the component's own value whatever the order, also one written after the loss, because the connect writes the pending loss. Read for `mx-link-button`'s `aria-disabled` with `disabled`, `mx-text-field`'s `aria-required` with `required`, and `mx-switch-button`'s `aria-checked`. `main` at `114270083` keeps them, so here the defect is wider since `RF-124`. Its ruling accepts it.
- **A template's value is the component's too.** `mx-switch-button`'s `aria-checked="false"` is in its template. A switch that isn't connected yet loses it when the host gets and loses the name across tasks, and nothing writes it until `checked` changes.
- **The order that loses in one task while out:** the loss, then the component's write, then the connect, in one task. The pending record is written by the connect, after the component's value. In a later task the value is kept.

#### RF-131 — An element whose slotted content changes while it is out of the document doesn't see the change, nor one that is built first and appended later

Tier A, **closed on 2026-11-25** (the last note), pre-existing. Before closure: open. Registered on 2026-11-24 by the architect, on `core/use-aria-1`, from `reviewer-5` of `RF-124`'s [recheck](reviews/aria-removed-1/feature-proof-recheck-claude.md), requested by the coordinator. `RF-130` is the highest `RF-` on any branch on `origin`, so this is the next free number. No entry covers it: `RF-124` is about the host's attributes, and `RF-75` and the button groups' entry are about which nodes `useSlot` passes. Read on built elements in Playwright's Chromium 158, Firefox 159 and WebKit 27.2, with the same result ([readings](aria-removed-1/checks/slot-out.txt), [probe](aria-removed-1/probes/slot-out.mjs)).

- **The cause.** Core's `useSlot` registers its `slotchange` listener through `useEvents`, which is active only while the host is connected. A slot dispatches the event also when its host is out of the document, in a microtask after the change. With no listener it is lost, and nothing asks for the content again at the connect.
- **What happens.** The report read a text field's label. The architect read the other callers, and two ways to meet it:

  | Element | Content changes while it is out, then it is put back | Made out with its content, appended in a later task |
  | --- | --- | --- |
  | `mx-text-field`, label | The old `aria-labelledby` stays, or none is set | **The control has no name from its label** |
  | `mx-text-field` and `mx-multiline-text-field`, support and counter | No `aria-describedby`, and **the text isn't shown** (56px high, not 76px) | The same |
  | `mx-connected-button-group` | With the first button removed, **no button is a tab stop**. An added button has no `tabindex` from the group. The end shapes are on the wrong buttons | **No roving tab stop and no end shapes at all** |
  | `mx-list-item` with a large image | 56px high, not 76px | The same |

  A button's icon, a standard group's first button and a sortable list's added item read as while connected, in what the probe compares. By reading, the standard group keeps the old list of buttons for its press effect, which the probe doesn't press. The sortable list reads its slot again when an item upgrades.

- **Why it is a problem:** building an element, waiting for something, and then appending it is ordinary. So is keeping an element and changing it out of the document. A control then has no name, or a group can't be reached with Tab. Where the change and the append are in one task, the event comes after the connect, and everything is right. That is why tests didn't find it.
- **Required properties:**
  1. After a connect, and after any later change, what an element says of its slotted content is what it would say if it had been connected at each change. It holds for a host that has never been connected.
  2. Each change is one call of the callback, as now, with the nodes that the slot has then. A connect adds no call, when nothing changed.
  3. The callback can run while the host is out of the document. `useSlot`'s JSDoc says so.
- **Direction, settled:** `useSlot` adds its listener to the slot once, when it is called, and not through `useEvents`. The slot is in the host's own shadow tree, so nothing outside keeps the host alive. Read with the listener replaced in the bundle: each of the 22 rows is as while connected, in the three engines (the same readings).
- **It changes a contract of core's public hook.** `useSlot.browser.test.ts` has _"should stop observing slot changes while host is disconnected"_ and _"should resume observing slot changes after host reconnect"_. The first says the opposite of property 1 and is replaced by a row for it. The second stays, with its expectation of what was missed corrected. **Not adopted: silent while out, with a call at the connect.** It would need a record of what was missed, or a call at each connect, also when nothing changed. None of the eight call sites in `src` needs the silence, by reading: `useRovingTabindex` reads `document.activeElement`, which finds no item of a host that is out, and the sortable list's controller is `null` then.
- **Rows:** in core, a change while out, a change before the first connect, and no call at a connect without a change. In material-x, each element and column of the table above. **Witness:** each fails before the repair, except the row without a change.
- **Order:** after `RF-124` merges, because the text field's rows read the same fallbacks. `useRovingTabindex`'s other users get it with the hook.
- **Not read:** Safari, screen readers, page-built callers of `useSlot`, and the sizes.
- **Plan needed:** no. **Ready** for an implementer, on a branch of its own. Nothing is the owner's to answer.
- **Size:** _small_.

#### RF-132 — A selected `mx-list-button-item` gives its button `aria-selected`, which the button role doesn't support

Tier A, **closed 2026-11-26** by #288 at `c7718d2ce` (the last note). Before closure: open, ready. Pre-existing. Registered on 2026-11-24 by the architect, on `repo/accessibility-findings-1`, from Mx Architect Explainer, relayed by the coordinator. The owner approved the registration (`RD-57` has his words). `RF-131` is the highest `RF-` on any branch on `origin`, so this is the next free number. Read at `eddf39e7b` ([readings](accessibility-findings-1/checks/axe-and-forced-colors.txt), [probe](accessibility-findings-1/probes/a11y.mjs.txt)).

- **What happens:** axe-core 4.14.1 reports `aria-allowed-attr`, critical, on the inner `<button>` of a selected `mx-list-button-item`, in Chromium, Firefox and WebKit. It reports nothing on an item that was never selected.
- **Cause:** core's `useSelectable` writes `aria-selected` on its target: `true` while `selected` is set, and `false` when it is removed. Core's own rows assert both.
- **Who is affected:** `mx-list-button-item` is the only adopter of `useSelectable` in `packages/*/src` (read). `mx-list-link-item` doesn't use it: it writes `aria-current="page"`, which every role supports, and axe reports nothing on it. The `Selectable` trait, which both have for the attribute, writes no ARIA.
- **Why it is a problem:** no assistive technology has to announce it. Chromium's tree exposes a selected item as a button with the same properties as one that isn't selected (read). Its selection is then only a color and a shape, and in forced colors not those either (`RF-133`).
- **Required property:** a selected `mx-list-button-item` gives its button no ARIA that the role doesn't support, and says that it is selected, or the record says that the page says it.
- **The replacement is the architect's ruling, and not the owner's.** The `@ydinjs` packages aren't on the registry, so core's hook can change or go with no compatibility to keep (`CONTRIBUTING.md` §8). The candidates:
  - **`aria-current="true"` while selected, and no attribute otherwise.** It is the architect's proposal. It is valid on a button, has no unselected value to choose, and the link item writes the same attribute. A page that has several selected items says _current_ for each, and ARIA asks for one in a set.
  - **`aria-pressed`.** It needs an explicit `false` for an unselected item, which `selected`, a boolean attribute, can't tell from an ordinary action. So the button would change between a toggle and a plain one.
  - **Nothing written by the component.** The page writes its own `aria-*` on the host, which `useARIA` mirrors.
- **Interaction:** `RF-130` is about a component's own value on the same control and reads `aria-selected` here. Its row changes with this repair, so the second to land merges the first. `RD-57`'s list names this violation, and the repair removes it there.
- **Rows:** the rule is gone, and a selected item says what the ruling gives. Core's `selectable.browser.test.ts` changes, or goes with the hook.
- **Order:** after `RD-57`, or before it with no list to edit. It doesn't wait for `RF-130`.
- **Not read:** a screen reader, Safari.
- **Plan needed:** no, only the ruling on the replacement.
- **Size:** _small_, after the ruling.

**Dated 2026-11-25 by the architect, on `material-x/list-selected-1`: the replacement is ruled, and the entry is ready for an implementer.** Requested by the coordinator. `main` at `8bed561de` is the base. Local labels, for Mx Architect to mint where one is wanted: `LS-1` to `LS-4`.

  - It is valid on a button, says nothing about an item that isn't selected, and is what the link item writes with `"page"`. The definition is the property: the element of a set that is visually styled as the current one. ARIA's _SHOULD NOT_ against `aria-current` in place of `aria-selected` is for widgets in which `aria-selected` has that meaning: gridcells, options, rows and tabs ([ARIA 1.2](https://www.w3.org/TR/wai-aria-1.2/#aria-current)).

A hook that writes `aria-selected` is right only for a role that supports it, and no component has one. `CONTRIBUTING.md` §8 gives no reason to keep an unused export: `@ydinjs/core` and `@ydinjs/material-x` aren't on the registry (read today, 404 for both). The entry says above that this ruling isn't the owner's, so nothing is asked.

A page whose items are toggles gives `aria-pressed` and `aria-current="false"` itself, and both reach the button. But `aria-pressed` stays on the host too, whose `listitem` role doesn't support it (`RF-94`), and axe asks for a review of it. So the documentation doesn't recommend it.
- **Not taken:** `aria-pressed` by the component (the entry's reason: without an explicit `false` the button changes from a toggle to a plain one, and with it every action is a toggle); nothing written by the component (a selected item is then a color); roles of a listbox (an option can't have the controls that an item's slots have, and the keyboard is another one); `useSelectable` kept in core with a value parameter (a mapping that only the list has).

#### RF-133 — material-x doesn't adapt to forced colors: a checked, selected or filled element loses what tells it apart

Tier A, **open**, pre-existing. Registered on 2026-11-24 by the architect, on `repo/accessibility-findings-1`, from Mx Architect Explainer, relayed by the coordinator. The owner approved the registration (`RD-57` has his words). `RF-132` is the entry before this one, so this is the next free number. Read at `eddf39e7b`, at rest, with Playwright's `forcedColors: 'active'` ([readings](accessibility-findings-1/checks/axe-and-forced-colors.txt), [Chromium](accessibility-findings-1/checks/forced-chromium.png), [Firefox](accessibility-findings-1/checks/forced-firefox.png), [probe](accessibility-findings-1/probes/a11y.mjs.txt)).

- **Corrected from the proposal:** material-x has forced-colors handling in one place, not none. The ripple draws nothing while the query matches (`ripple.ts` and its stylesheet), and no test of material-x emulates forced colors. The proposal hadn't read the selected radio, the switch buttons, the FAB, the text field, the card, the list or a resting button. They are read here. The [card's reviews](reviews/card-1/checks/forced-colors.txt) and the focus indicators' read forced colors before.
- **What happens.** Forced colors replace `background-color`, and Material's containers and states are drawn with it.

  | Element | Chromium | Firefox |
  | --- | --- | --- |
  | Checkbox, checked or indeterminate | No box, only the mark | The same |
  | Filled, tonal and elevated button, filled icon button, FAB, split button | No container, no outline. The three buttons are identical to a text button, and the filled icon button to a text one | A container in one color. The three buttons are identical |
  | `mx-link-button`, filled | No container | No container |
  | `mx-switch-button`, checked and not | **Identical** | Only the corner shape differs |
  | `mx-switch-icon-button`, checked and not | **Identical** | **Identical** |
  | Connected group, the checked button and the other | No containers, so no difference (screenshot) | One color, so only the corners differ (screenshot) |
  | `mx-list-button-item`, selected and not | **Identical** | Only the corner shape differs |
  | `mx-list-link-item`, selected and not | **Identical** | **Identical** |
  | Text field with `error` and without | **Identical** | **Identical** |
  | Filled and elevated card | No edge, only the text | The same |
  | Radio, selected and not; outlined button, card and text field; checkbox unchecked | Drawn, and the radio's states differ | The same |

  Identical means the same pixels in the element's box. Each pair differs without forced colors.

- **Why it is a problem:** a user with a high-contrast theme, such as Windows' contrast themes, can't see whether a switch is on, which list item is selected or whether a field has an error, and a checked checkbox has no edge.
- **Required properties,** for the plan to complete:
  1. Under forced colors, each state that Material gives an element a different appearance for stays visible without color alone: checked, selected, disabled and error.
  2. A control keeps a visible edge or container, as it does where its outline is drawn.
  3. Colors come from system colors. Without the preference nothing changes.
- **The survey comes first,** on every element and state, and not only at rest: hovered, pressed, focused, disabled, selected radio with each state, multiline and outlined text fields, the split button open, the sortable list while a drag is in flight, and a high-contrast theme in both color schemes. The probe here has 35 elements and states at rest. WebKit's emulation forces no color, so it can't be read there.
- **The elements that aren't all on `main`:** `mx-card` is on `main` (its outline is read, above). `mx-slider` is on `material-x/slider-1` (#220) and has its own rule, which takes system colors for its parts, with visual rows and a command that emulates forced colors, `emulateForcedColors`. `mx-top-app-bar` is on `material-x/top-app-bar-1` (#211) and has none. The survey starts with the slider's rule, because the package's approach should be one.
- **Tests** go with it, through the slider's command once it merges.
- **RTL** is beside it and not in it: `RF-134`.
- **Order:** after #220 merges, so that its command and its rule are the starting point. It doesn't wait for `RF-132`, whose selection is what a list item's forced-colors row would show.
- **Not read:** Windows itself, Safari, a real contrast theme. Emulation is Chromium's and Firefox's, and the two don't agree on a button.
- **Plan needed:** yes, by the architect, after the survey. Nothing is the owner's to answer now.
- **Size:** _large_.

#### RF-134 — In right-to-left text, a connected group's and a split button's outer corners are on the inner side, and no test covers the groups

Tier A, **open**, pre-existing. Until the last note, of 2026-11-24, it was Tier B, with the title _No test covers the button groups in right-to-left text_. Registered on 2026-11-24 by the architect, on `repo/accessibility-findings-1`, from Mx Architect Explainer, relayed by the coordinator. The owner approved the registration (`RD-57` has his words). `RF-133` is the entry before this one, so this is the next free number. Read at `eddf39e7b`, by searching `packages/material-x/tests` for `rtl` and `direction`.

- **What is missing:** no row in material-x observes `mx-button-group`, `mx-connected-button-group` or `mx-split-button` under RTL. The sortable list is the only element with one. Core's `useRovingTabindex` has rows for the arrow keys, and no row reads them through a group.
- **What could break and not be seen:** the connected group's end shapes, the standard group's neighbors that widen when one is pressed, and the roving order. By reading, the standard group's `padding-inline` follows the direction, and `LEADING`/`TRAILING` props are logical.
- **Required property:** in RTL, the first button of a group has its outer corners at the inline start, the press widens toward the correct side, and the arrow keys follow what is seen.
- **Rows,** in each engine at `RD-20`'s floor: the connected group's corners, the standard group's press and the arrow keys, for `dir` on the group and on an ancestor. **Witness:** a deliberate reversal of the mapping fails them.
- **Other elements:** the slider and the top app bar have RTL rows on their branches. Which of the rest need them is the survey's to say (`RF-133`), because both are per-element sweeps. This entry covers the groups only.
- **Order:** it waits for nothing.
- **Plan needed:** no. **Size:** _medium_.

**Dated 2026-11-24 by the architect, on `material-x/group-focus-1`: the required property fails today,** on an observation in `RF-126`'s [feature proof](reviews/group-focus-1/feature-proof-claude.md), relayed by the coordinator, and read again on the built elements in the three engines, which agree ([reading](focus-cover-1/checks/rtl-groups.txt), [probe](focus-cover-1/probes/rtl-groups.mjs)). The branch doesn't change it.

- **The corners, a defect:** with `dir="rtl"` on the group or on an ancestor, the first button of `mx-connected-button-group` is at the right and has its outer corners (20px) at its left, and the last one, at the left, has them at its right. So each end of the group has the inner corners, and the outer corners face the neighbor. `mx-split-button` is the same. The cause is in `connected/main.styles.css`: `--_border-radius` for `data-first` and `data-last` is a value of `border-radius`, whose four corners are physical.
- **The arrow keys are right:** in the connected group ArrowRight moves to the right and ArrowLeft to the left, in both directions. In `mx-button-group` no arrow moved the focus in either direction, so that part of the property has no subject there.
- **The standard group's press can't be read:** it changes no width in LTR either, which is `RF-80`'s. So that part waits for `RF-80`, and the rest waits for nothing. _"Order: it waits for nothing"_ above is read so.
- **The tier is A,** because a consumer in RTL sees another shape, and the title says the defect.
- **The required property adds:** in RTL, a connected group's last button and a split button's two have their outer corners at the outer side, at rest, selected and pressed.
- **Rows:** the corners of the first and the last button of the connected group and of the split button's two, and the connected group's arrow keys. The corner rows fail before the repair, which is their witness.
- **The repair's form** is the implementer's. `--md-button-group-inner-corner-size` works as it does, in both directions.
- **`RF-126` isn't affected:** its indicator is whole in RTL by the proof's pixels, and follows the button's shape.
- **Plan needed:** no. **Ready** for an implementer. **Size:** _medium_, unchanged: the repair is a few lines, and the rows are the rest.

**Dated 2026-11-25 by the implementer, on `material-x/group-rtl-1`: the corners follow the group's direction.** `main` at `ee0afea12` is the base. By the owner's rule of 2026-11-25, relayed by the coordinator, only Chromium was read.

- **Form:** two rules in `connected/main.styles.css`, in `:host(:dir(rtl))`: the first and the last button exchange their values. The split button's corners are the connected group's, so its sheet doesn't change.
- **Why not logical corner properties on the button:** they follow the member's own direction, so a member with another `dir`, such as a label with `dir="auto"`, would turn its corners in a group that is right today. They would also add to the sheet of every button.
- **Limit:** `:dir()` reads the `dir` attribute, on the group or an ancestor, through shadow roots. A page's CSS `direction` without `dir` mirrors the layout and the arrow keys and leaves the corners as they are on `main`. The required property names `dir` alone.
- **Pressed:** a pressed button's outer corners are its own pressed shape (8px in the small size), in LTR also. The split button's trailing button is a pill while pressed or open, and a selected button is a pill, so those rows hold in both directions and tell nothing apart. A selected button that is pressed does.
- **With `RF-143` (#287):** its `::slotted([data-first][data-last])` stands in both directions, because the rules here leave out a member that is both. On this branch, the only member of a group still has the last button's corners of LTR, in both directions, as on `main`.
- **Rows:** 66 in `button-group-rtl.spec.browser.test.ts`: no `dir`, `dir="rtl"` on the group, on an ancestor, and an LTR group in an RTL ancestor; at rest, pressed, selected, both, and with `--md-button-group-inner-corner-size`; a `dir` that changes; a member with another `dir`; the split button at rest, pressed and open. Six of the arrow keys in `button-group-rtl.browser.test.ts`. The standard group's press isn't here (`RF-80`).
- **Witnesses** ([reading](group-rtl-1/checks/witnesses.txt), [program](group-rtl-1/probes/mutate.mjs)), of 72 rows, failed: `main`'s sheet 26; the directions reversed 50; always reversed 30; only a `dir` attribute on the group 14; no rule for the first button 14, for the last 12; the member's direction 4; the override ignored 4; the arrow keys reversed 6, and without a direction 4; none without a mutation.
- **Checks,** Chromium: core 364 passed; material-x without the visual project 2114 passed and 2 expected failures. The root format check, typecheck, lint, size gate, publint, `docs-build` and `docs-smoke` (129 of 129) pass.
- **Sizes,** Brotli, one reading each, `main`'s sheet then the head's: `button-group/connected-button-group` 4042 to 4069, `button/split-button` 7766 to 7796, `complete` 25924 to 25980. The other 33 rows are the same, and none of the three has a limit.
- **Not run:** Firefox, WebKit, Safari, the visual project, the declarations' typecheck, and the entry's probe on the built groups. No visual baseline is of RTL.
- **For the reviewer:** `:host(:dir(rtl))` with a `dir` that changes after the render, and the group in the split button's shadow root, are where an engine could differ.

**Dated 2026-11-26 by the architect: the [feature proof](reviews/group-rtl-1/feature-proof-claude.md) of `71b839f4a` is triaged,** requested by the coordinator. Read from the proof and its readings, with no run of my own. The required property holds in the three engines, and both findings are accepted.

- **`reviewer-1`, accepted, for the implementer.** The list of rows named the first and the last button, and what a consumer sees also depends on the two guards that no row reads. **Rows owed,** in `button-group-rtl.spec.browser.test.ts`:
  1. In an RTL group of three members, the middle one has four inner corners, at rest.
  2. **The only member of a group has the same corners in RTL as in LTR.** The row compares the two directions and names no value, so it holds before `RF-143` (#287) reaches `main` and after: today both are 8, 8, 20, 20, and with `RF-143`'s `::slotted([data-first][data-last])` both are outer on all sides. Whichever unit merges second keeps it passing.

  **Witnesses:** the proof's two mutations, `[data-first]` out of the RTL first-button rule and `:not([data-first])` out of the RTL last-button rule, each fail one of them. Neither depends on an engine, so they are developed and witnessed in Chromium (`RD-62`).

- **`reviewer-2`, accepted, as a limit published in the package.** The corners follow the `dir` attribute, as the required property's rows name, and not a page's CSS `direction` alone. **Why not the computed direction:** `:dir()` is the one selector for it, and reads `dir` alone. Logical corner properties on the member follow the member's own direction, so a member with another `dir`, such as a label with `dir="auto"`, would turn its corners in a group that is right. A script read of the computed `direction` hears no change of it. CSS Writing Modes asks HTML documents to set the direction with `dir` and not with the `direction` property, so a page that follows it sees the right corners. **The arrow keys stay as they are:** they follow the computed direction, so they follow what is seen in both cases, and that is the property's own words. **Text owed,** in `connected-button-group.mdx` and `split-button.mdx`, a bullet in their behavior lists: _"**Direction:** the outer corners follow the `dir` attribute on the group or an ancestor. #### RF-135 — A list item's trail slot clips the focus indicator of what is in it, and in Firefox all of it

Tier A, **closed on 2026-11-25** (the last note), pre-existing. Before closure: open. Registered on 2026-11-24 by the architect, on `material-x/handle-focus-1`, from the implementer's return of `RF-128`, on the coordinator's question whether it is a finding of its own. `RF-134` is the highest `RF-` on any branch on `origin` and in the local slots, so this is the next free number. Read at `751b1fb81` merged, on the built elements in Playwright's Chromium 158, Firefox 159 and WebKit 27.2 ([reading](handle-focus-1/checks/trail-focus.txt), [probe](handle-focus-1/probes/trail-focus.mjs)).

- **What happens:** `.trail` has `overflow: hidden` and fits its content, so the indicator, which lies 2px outside the control, is cut. In a plain `mx-list` with a static item, the indicator's own pixels, whole in `lead` and cut in `trail`:

  | Control in the slot | Chromium, lead / trail | Firefox | WebKit |
  | --- | --- | --- | --- |
  | `mx-icon-button` | 324 / **92** | 321 / **0** | 317 / **92** |
  | `mx-icon-button`, xsmall | 271 / **54** | 296 / **0** | 275 / **54** |
  | `mx-button` | 330 / **92** | 327 / **0** | 319 / **92** |
  | `mx-checkbox` | 324 / **92** | 321 / **0** | 317 / **92** |

  A page's own button, link or `tabindex` element loses the browser's outline in the same way: in Firefox a `tabindex` on `mx-icon` shows none of it in `trail`. What focus changes there besides is the item's own focused shape (`:focus-within`), about 200 pixels at its corners, and, on a package button, its state layer.

- **Why it matters:** the controls in `trail` are the ordinary ones, and the story has an `mx-icon-button` there. A keyboard user in Firefox doesn't see which control has focus.
- **Required property:** nothing of a list item covers or cuts a pixel of the focus indicator of a control in its `lead` or `trail` slot. Content that a page puts in `trail` keeps its layout.
- **Direction:** the clip goes, as `RF-128`'s last note reads and orders, with its rows. The two are one unit, because a rule for `RF-128` alone makes a trailing handle worse.
- **Costs:** what that note says of a page's bounded child.
- **Plan needed:** no. **Ready.** The owner's approval of the start is for the coordinator to ask. **Size:** _small_.

**Dated 2026-11-25 by the architect:** the property holds by the [feature proof](reviews/handle-focus-1/feature-proof-claude.md), and nothing is owed here. `RF-128`'s note of this day has the rulings for both. `reviewer-3`'s mutation of `align-content` gets no row, and `reviewer-4` is answered there.

**Closed 2026-11-25 by the architect,** with `RF-128`, whose last note has the reading and the condition.

#### RF-136 — The split button's trailing button is named by its icon's ligature, can't be given a name, and doesn't expose `open`

Tier A, **closed on 2026-11-25** (the last note), pre-existing. Before closure: open, ready. Registered on 2026-11-24 by the architect, on `repo/records-batch-1`, from [#243](https://github.com/ausginer/material-x/issues/243), relayed by the coordinator. It was seen when `RD-57` was registered. `RF-135` is on `material-x/handle-focus-1`, so this is the next free number. Read at `4e2972514`, on the built elements, in each engine's own accessibility tree, in Playwright's Chromium 158, Firefox 159 and WebKit 27.2, which agree ([Chromium](records-batch-1/checks/names-chromium.txt), [Firefox](records-batch-1/checks/names-firefox.txt), [WebKit](records-batch-1/checks/names-webkit.txt), [probe](records-batch-1/probes/names.ts)).

- **What happens (the name):** the trailing button is a `button` named `keyboard_arrow_down`, the text of the `mx-icon` in the template. `RD-57` read it in Chromium only. `aria-label` on the host leaves the two buttons as they are, and names the host itself, `generic` in Chromium and Firefox and `group` in WebKit. There is no slot, attribute or property for the trailing button's name, and a part can't carry one.
- **What happens (the state):** the trailing button has no expanded state, with `open` and without. `open` sets only the custom state `open`, which the styles read. A host `aria-expanded` or `aria-haspopup` doesn't reach the button. The split button's page says that _"`open` and `secondaryaction` communicate expanded/collapsed secondary action state"_, and to assistive technology `open` communicates nothing. The controls of the probe, a native `<button aria-expanded aria-haspopup>`, read as expanded in Chromium and Firefox, and as a pop-up button in WebKit. Its expanded state didn't come back through WebKit's protocol, so WebKit's row has the attribute's absence on the button and not a reading of the state.
- **Why it is a problem:** a screen reader would announce an icon's name in place of the action, in English on any page, and doesn't say whether the menu is open. The page's author can't repair either.
- **Not affected:** the leading button. It is named by its content.
- **Required properties:**
  1. The trailing button's accessible name is the page's to give, in the page's language, and no icon's text is part of it.
  2. The trailing button exposes `open` as its expanded state, from the first render and at each change: `false` without `open`, `true` with it.
  3. A host `aria-label` doesn't name the trailing button, because the host has two.
- **Property 2 adds no public surface,** so it is ruled here. `aria-haspopup` and `aria-controls` aren't set: what opens is the page's. A split button whose `secondaryaction` opens nothing has `aria-expanded="false"` as well. The documentation calls the trailing button a toggle.
- **Precedent, read:** Material Components for Android at `6061a6991` sets the trailing button's state description to _Expanded_ or _Collapsed_, and leaves its name to the app, as `android:contentDescription` in its example. Material's pages weren't read.
- **Q1, for the owner — how does a page name the trailing button?**
  - **(a) An attribute and property for it, `secondarylabel`, with no default. Recommended.** It goes to the trailing button as its name, beside `secondaryaction`. The documentation says that it is required. Without it the button has no name, which axe-core's `button-name` reports (`RD-57`), and the ligature hides from that rule today. The name of the attribute is the architect's proposal.
  - (b) (a), with an English default such as _More options_. The button is never unnamed. A page in another language that forgets it has an English name, and the string is in every bundle. `mx-sortable-list` has English defaults for its handle, which the page overrides on its own element.
  - (c) A slot for the trailing button's content, whose named icon names it. It also lets a page change the icon. The named icon (`role="img"` with `aria-label`) does name a button today (read). It is more surface than the name needs, and the icon's turn on `open` would apply to a page's content.
  - (d) Nothing in the API. The trailing button takes a name from the leading one's label, so that two buttons have one name and differ by the expanded state.
- **Order:** property 2 waits for nothing, and property 1 for Q1. One unit does both. Its name's second node is `RF-94`'s: an `aria-label` on the inner `mx-icon-button` names that element too. If `RF-137` lands first without this, the trailing button has no name, so **this one goes before `RF-137` or with it.**
- **Rows,** each engine's own accessibility tree, as `RF-94` says: the name with and without the label, the expanded state in both states, and a change of `open`. **Witness:** they fail before the repair.
- **Plan needed:** no, once Q1 is answered. A new attribute is public surface, so the answer is minted as a decision. **Size:** _medium_.

**Dated 2026-11-25 by the architect: Q1 is answered by the owner, (a), on 2026-11-24, and it is `RD-58`.** In chat, relayed by the coordinator: _"Q1-Q3: (a), да на RF-138 и RF-140"_ ("Q1-Q3: (a), yes to RF-138 and RF-140"). **Ready** for an implementer, on `material-x/split-button-names-1`, in one unit with `RF-138`. #### RF-137 — An `mx-icon`'s ligature text is part of the name of the control that it is in

Tier A, **open**, **ready** (the last note), pre-existing. Registered on 2026-11-24 by the architect, on `repo/records-batch-1`, from the reading that `RF-136` asked for. `RF-136` is the entry before this one. Read as `RF-136`, with the same probe.

- **What happens:** with `<mx-icon>edit</mx-icon>` and the label _Save_, in Chromium, Firefox and WebKit:

  | Element | Accessible name |
  | --- | --- |
  | `mx-button`, `mx-link-button`, `mx-switch-button`, extended `mx-fab`, and the split button's leading button, with the icon in `icon` | `edit Save` |
  | `mx-list-button-item` and `mx-list-link-item`, with icons in `lead` and `trail` | `edit Save edit` |
  | `mx-icon-button`, `mx-switch-icon-button` and `mx-fab` with the icon alone | `edit` |
  | Any of them with a host `aria-label` | The label |
  | A text field with a label and icons in `lead` and `trail` | `Save` |

  A static list item and an `mx-icon` alone expose the text as text (Firefox's tree; WebKit's name of the list item has it too). The checkbox's and the radio's own icons are hidden in their templates.

- **What the documentation says:** `icon.mdx` tells the page to set `aria-hidden="true"` on a decorative icon. That works: the name is `Save`. No page, story or usage snippet of material-x does so, on any `mx-icon`.
- **Why it is a problem:** a screen reader says _edit Save_, and _chevron_right_ at the end of a list item. The voice user who says the visible label still matches, because the label is in the name. The ligature isn't seen by anybody, so it isn't content.
- **Required property:** in each engine at `RD-20`'s floor, the text of an `mx-icon` is in no accessible name and no accessible text, and a page can still give an icon a name of its own, which is then part of its control's name.
- **Candidates, read in the three engines:**
  - **The slot inside a `<span aria-hidden="true">` in the icon's shadow tree:** every name above is without the icon's text, and `role="img" aria-label="Draft"` on the icon still gives `Draft Save`.
  - `aria-hidden="true"` on the slot itself: the same in Chromium and Firefox. WebKit ignores it, so its names don't change.
  - The internals' `ariaHidden` on the host: the names are without the text, and `role="img"` with a label no longer gives the icon a name, in any engine.
  - material-web at `268681913` writes the attribute `aria-hidden="true"` on the icon's host, and a page that writes `false` gets it removed. It edits the page's attribute. Read in its source, and not run.
- **Q2, for the owner — is an `mx-icon`'s text hidden by the package?**
  - **(a) Yes, by the first candidate. Recommended.** A page can't get it wrong, and an icon with a meaning takes `role="img"` and `aria-label`. **Cost:** an icon-only control without `aria-label` has no name, where today it has the ligature. The pages of the two icon buttons already ask for `aria-label`, and the FAB's asks for it when the icon is ambiguous. An SVG or text with a meaning inside an `mx-icon` is hidden too. One element for each icon, whose size, layout and speed weren't measured.
  - (b) No: it stays the page's, and material-x's pages, stories and snippets gain `aria-hidden="true"`. No code changes. Each page has to know it, and the split button's template hides its own icon.
  - (c) The package hides it only in the `icon`, `lead` and `trail` slots of its elements. An icon-only button keeps its ligature name. It is more code than (a), and an icon outside those slots is as today.
- **Order:** after `RF-136` or with it. It doesn't wait for `RF-94`.
- **Rows,** each engine's own tree: the rows of the table, the named icon, and an icon alone. **Witness:** they fail before the repair. Pixels: no visual baseline changes.

  - **The cause, read in Gecko's source** (`DocAccessible.cpp`, the head of `main` of 2026-11-25, which isn't the version that was run): `PruneOrInsertSubtree` removes an accessible that has lost its frame, and doesn't ask whether its new ancestors are `aria-hidden`. So a leaf made before the upgrade stays when its text moves into a subtree that is hidden from the start. `AttributeChanged` calls `ContentRemoved` on the element when its `aria-hidden` becomes true. That removes the leaves, through the slot's assigned nodes. So the attribute has to change after the slot has its nodes, and it doesn't have to be later than that.
  - **It is wider than the stop says: names fail too.** In the control, with the button defined 400 ms before the icon, `x-button` is `edit Save` with the template's `aria-hidden`, 3 of 3. A native button with the icon is `edit` in each late order.

#### RF-138 — A disabled split button isn't disabled

Tier A, **closed on 2026-11-25** (the last note), pre-existing. Before closure: open. Registered on 2026-11-24 by the architect, on `repo/records-batch-1`, from `RF-136`'s reading, whose rows for a disabled split button differed between the engines. `RF-137` is the entry before this one. Run at `4e2972514`, on the built elements, in Playwright's Chromium 158, Firefox 159 and WebKit 27.2 ([reading](records-batch-1/checks/split-disabled.txt), [probe](records-batch-1/probes/split-disabled.mjs)).

- **What happens,** with `disabled` in the markup or set later, or in a disabled fieldset, the same in the three engines except where said:
  - neither inner button is `disabled`, and neither has the disabled state or look. The background is the enabled one;
  - **a click on the trailing button fires `secondaryaction`;**
  - a click on the leading button gives no `click` on the host, only because the host is a disabled form-associated element;
  - Tab reaches both buttons. Enter on the trailing one fires `secondaryaction`. Enter on the leading one fires `click` in Chromium, and nothing in the other two.
  - Chromium's tree exposes both buttons as disabled, from the host. Firefox's and WebKit's don't.
- **What is documented:** `@attr disabled` is _"Disables both actions"_, and the page says that _"`disabled` disables both split action segments"_.
- **The cause:** the constructor transfers `BUTTON_ATTRS` to the inner group, and those are `color`, `size` and `shape`. `disabled` is in `DISABLEABLE_ATTRS`, which it doesn't take. When this began wasn't read.
- **Why it is a problem:** a page that disables the split button while it works still gets the secondary action, and its user sees an enabled control.
- **Required property:** with `disabled` on the split button, both inner buttons are natively disabled, take no focus and no activation, fire nothing, and draw the disabled appearance. Without it they return. The group's other attributes keep working.
- **A candidate that holds, read:** with the host and the inner group both `disabled`, the property holds in the three engines: no focus, no event, the disabled background. `ButtonCore` already takes the group's `disabled`.
- **The fieldset is `RF-119`'s,** which hadn't read this element. This entry doesn't wait for it.
- **Rows,** in each engine: for the attribute, the property and their removal, `disabled` on both inner buttons, no focus by Tab, no event from a click and from the keyboard on each button, and the disabled colors. **Witness:** without the transfer they fail. The `open` and `secondaryaction` rows that exist pass unchanged.
- **Plan needed:** no. **Ready** for an implementer, in `RF-136`'s unit (below). **Size:** _small_.

#### RF-139 — A list item's long texts run out of it, and two trailing children stack

Tier A, **open**, **remediation owed** (the architect's note of 2026-11-26), with properties 1 to 4 narrowed, pre-existing. Registered on 2026-11-24 by the architect, on `repo/records-batch-1`, from [#254](https://github.com/ausginer/material-x/issues/254), relayed by the coordinator. It was seen in `RF-128`'s reading of the trail slot's clip, on `material-x/handle-focus-1`. `RF-138` is the entry before this one. Read at `4e2972514`, on the built elements, in a 300 px list, on static and button items, in Playwright's Chromium 158, Firefox 159 and WebKit 27.2 ([reading](records-batch-1/checks/trail-long.txt), [probe](records-batch-1/probes/trail-long.mjs)).

- **What happens,** in each engine. The widths differ by the fallback font:
  - **Long trailing text** stays on one line and runs out of the item: 35 px past its end in Chromium, 57 px in Firefox and WebKit, with a text that is 268 to 289 px wide. Nothing shortens it. The slot's `text-overflow: ellipsis` never applies, because the slot is as wide as its content.
  - **It squeezes the label.** A label of several words beside it gets 49 to 54 px, one word to a line, and the item is 308 to 380 px high, where a short trailing text leaves it at 92 px.
  - **One long word as the label** runs out too, and pushes the trailing text 212 to 266 px past the item's end. `.content` has no smaller minimum than its longest word. The page, 400 px wide, gets a horizontal scroll.
  - **Two trailing children stack:** two icons are 20 × 40 px, two icon buttons 40 × 80 px in an item of 100 px, and a text and an icon are one above the other. Two texts stay on a line.
- **The cause:** `.trail` is `flex: 0 0 min-content`, so it doesn't shrink, and it is as narrow as its content allows. Slotted text is `white-space: nowrap`. `.content` keeps the automatic minimum.
- **With `RF-135`'s repair,** which removes the slot's clip, every box is the same, read here as `noclip`.
- **Why it is a problem:** a date, an amount or a name that is longer than expected covers what is beside the list or gives the page a scroll, and two trailing actions make a tall item.
- **Required properties:**
  1. No text of a list item, in any slot, runs past the item's end, and none adds a scroll to the page.
  2. A long text in one slot doesn't take the other's whole width: the label and the trailing text stay readable.
  3. Trailing children are side by side while the item has room.
  4. Short texts, icons, and controls keep their boxes, and a control in `trail` isn't narrowed, cut or clipped (`RF-135`).
- **Candidates, read:**

  | Rule | Long trailing text | Long label, short text | One long word as the label | Two icon buttons |
  | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
  | The slot may shrink, text on one line (`shrink`) | Past the end | The trailing text is 13 px wide in Chromium, of 28 | Past the end | Side by side |
  | The slot may shrink and the text wraps (`wrap`) | Two lines | The trailing text is 13 px wide in Chromium, broken in three lines | Past the end | Side by side |
  | The slot may shrink and the slotted element clips with an ellipsis (`ellipsis`) | One line, ellipsis | Cut to 13 px in Chromium | Past the end | Stacked: the element becomes a block |
  | **`bound`:** `.content` starts from zero with no minimum, `.trail` is its content's width up to half of the item, the text wraps and a long word breaks | 2 or 3 lines in the item | Unchanged | In the item, with the label's own ellipsis | Side by side |

  Only `bound` has nothing past the end in any of the 13 contents, both kinds of item and the three engines, and it keeps the boxes of short texts, icons, a checkbox and a button. Its cost: a trailing text of more than half of the item wraps, also beside a short label, where it fits on one line today.

- **Q3, for the owner — what does a trailing text do when it is too long?**
  - **(a) It wraps, and takes up to half of the item. Recommended:** the whole text is seen, and nothing is clipped, so it doesn't conflict with `RF-135`. It is `bound`.
  - (b) It stays on one line and ends with an ellipsis. The text is then cut on the page's element, whose own clip cuts a focus indicator inside it, and a control can't be told from a text there. It needs a rule for which children it applies to.
  - (c) It stays as it is, documented: a page bounds its own trailing text. Properties 1 and 2 then hold for the label only.
- **The other properties don't wait for Q3's answer in substance,** but they are the same three declarations, so one unit does all of it.
- **Not established:** what Material says. `md.comp.list` has no token for it. material-web's item (`268681913`) doesn't shrink its trailing slot either, and clips the host. Material's pages weren't read. Also not read: RTL, 200 % text, the link item, the sortable list, a supporting text and an overline that are long.
- **Order:** after `material-x/handle-focus-1` merges, because `RF-135` edits the same rules. It doesn't wait for `RF-64`, whose subject is the support slot's line count.

**Dated 2026-11-26 by the architect: the recheck's finding is accepted, and the declaration stays. `mx-button`'s pages say that its label keeps its words, and rows hold it outside a list.** Requested by the coordinator. The recheck is [`recheck-claude.md`](reviews/item-overflow-1/recheck-claude.md), of `c7b7a3e32`, committed in `c58f0eac6`. It finds the remediation as ruled in the three engines, and the departure in row 2 is accepted there. Nothing was probed again. Nothing is the owner's: the choice keeps the last note's ruling, that a control owns its words, and he is told it with its cost.

- **`recheck-1`, accepted.** The declaration is in the sheet that `ButtonCore` adopts, so `mx-button`, `mx-link-button`, `mx-switch-button` and the split button's leading button keep their labels' words in any container, not only in a list item. A page's `overflow-wrap`, on a container or on the element, doesn't reach the label. `::part(impl)` does, and `word-break` does ([Chromium](reviews/item-overflow-1/checks/recheck-outside-chromium.txt), [Firefox](reviews/item-overflow-1/checks/recheck-outside-firefox.txt), [WebKit](reviews/item-overflow-1/checks/recheck-outside-webkit.txt)). No text said so.
- **The ruling: the button owns its label's breaks inside words, everywhere.** Its `.host` already sets the label's font, its size and its alignment, so its line breaking is the button's too. A label broken inside its words is unreadable wherever it is, which is the last note's reason, and isn't a property of the list. **The cost:** a page that let a button's label break inside its words to keep the button in a narrow container sees the button run out of it, by 35 to 36px with _Download_ in 60px. With the break the label's lines run out of the 40px box instead, by 16 to 17px. The page that wants the break sets `overflow-wrap` on `::part(impl)`, a documented part.
- **`word-break` keeps reaching the label, on purpose.** It carries a script's rules, such as `keep-all`, which keeps a Korean word whole, and a button that reset it would break such a label between its syllables. `overflow-wrap` is only the break of a word that doesn't fit.
- **Not adopted: the declaration in the list item,** by `::slotted` rules that name each control of the library. The list would have to know every control with a text label, and outside a list a narrow container would break a label inside its words, as on `main`.
- **Owed by the implementer,** on `material-x/item-overflow-1`:
  1. **Texts.** In the _Anatomy_ of `button.mdx`, `link-button.mdx`, `switch-button.mdx` and `split-button.mdx`, one sentence each: the label breaks between its words and never inside one, whatever `overflow-wrap` its container or the element has. To let it break inside words, a page sets `overflow-wrap` on `::part(impl)`, or on `::part(leading-impl)` for the split button's leading button. `word-break` still applies.
  2. **Rows,** in the three engines, on `mx-button`, `mx-link-button` and `mx-switch-button`: _Download_ in a 60px container. With `overflow-wrap: anywhere` on the container, and with it on the element, the label has one line and the element is at least the word's width. With it on `::part(impl)`, the label has more than one line and the element is at most 60px wide. **Witness:** with `overflow-wrap: inherit` on `.host`, the first two rows fail. The third row holds what the page is told, and is the platform's.
  3. **No source change.** The size gate is unchanged.
  4. **The description of #286** says that a button's label keeps its words, in a list and outside one, so the owner reads it there.
- **No recheck is owed:** four sentences and rows whose witness the coordinator reads in the implementer's report. CI runs the rows in Firefox and WebKit.

**Dated 2026-11-26 by the implementer, on `material-x/item-overflow-1`: the texts and the rows are in.** Requested by the coordinator. Chromium alone (`RD-62`).

- **Texts:** the sentence is in the _Anatomy_ of `button.mdx`, `link-button.mdx` and `switch-button.mdx`, with `::part(impl)`, and of `split-button.mdx`, for its leading button, with `::part(leading-impl)`.
- **Rows:** 9 in `tests/button/button-label-breaks.browser.test.ts`, three on each of `mx-button`, `mx-link-button` and `mx-switch-button`. _Download_ is in a 60px container. With `overflow-wrap: anywhere` on the container, and with it on the element, the label has one line, and the element is wider than 60px and at least as wide as the label's text without a container. With it on `::part(impl)`, the label has more than one line, and the element is at most 60px wide.

#### RF-141 — A button that is upgraded after the connected group's last slot change isn't in its roving order

Tier A, **closed on 2026-11-25** (the architect's last note, whose list the note after it completes), pre-existing. Before closure: open. Registered on 2026-11-25 by the architect, on `core/slot-listener-1`, from `reviewer-1` of `RF-131`'s [feature proof](reviews/slot-listener-1/feature-proof-claude.md), requested by the coordinator. `RF-140` is the highest `RF-` on any branch on `origin`, so this is the next free number. No entry covers it: `RF-69` is about a consumer that is there before its provider, and `RF-131` about a slot change that is lost. Read at `96442bad3` with `main` at `a110683b3`, in Playwright's Chromium, Firefox and WebKit, with the same result ([reading](slot-listener-1/checks/ruling.txt), [probe](reviews/slot-listener-1/probes/callers.browser.test.ts.txt)). The former `useSlot` reads the same.

- **The cause.** `useRovingTabindex` keeps the slot's nodes that are items, at each `slotchange`. A node that isn't upgraded yet isn't an item, and its upgrade is no slot change. So it stays out until the next one.
- **What happens,** in `mx-connected-button-group`, the hook's only user:
  - **Buttons from `template.content.cloneNode(true)`,** appended to a group that is out or not yet connected. The group is connected in a later task. No button has a `tabindex`, each is a tab stop, and the arrow keys do nothing. With one clone among created buttons, or a clone in place of the first, the same: the clone has no `tabindex`, or the group has no managed tab stop. Connected, the same content reads right, because a connected clone is upgraded before the slot's event.
  - **Buttons whose module is evaluated in a later task than the group's,** with the group connected: none has a `tabindex`. A page that loads the group and the buttons as separate modules, or the buttons by `import()`, meets it.
  - The end shapes are right, because they don't need an upgrade. `innerHTML`, `importNode` and `createElement` upgrade at once, and read right.
- **Why it is a problem:** both are ordinary ways to build a page, and a keyboard user gets three tab stops and no arrow keys. The sortable list has neither: it reads its slot again when an item asks for its context.
- **Required properties:**
  1. A button that is in the group's slot is in its roving order once it is an item, however late it is upgraded and wherever the group is then. It doesn't need another slot change. The tab stop then is what it would be if the button had been an item at the slot change.
  2. A node that leaves the slot before it is upgraded is never in the order and gets no `tabindex`. A node that is never defined changes nothing.
- **Direction, settled:** `useRovingTabindex`'s slot callback also waits for the definition of each slotted element that isn't defined, upgrades that element and reads the slot again. Read as a [candidate](slot-listener-1/probes/roving-candidate.diff) in the three engines: 0 of the 126 readings differ, where nine do without it, the arrow keys walk, and the late items read `0` and `-1`. In both cases the same wait answers: for a clone the name is already defined, so the upgrade comes a microtask after the slot's call. It isn't prescribed.
- **Not adopted.** A second read at the connect: the children are upgraded after the group's `connected`, and late definitions aren't answered. The context that the sortable list uses: the hook is core's and knows no group, and the group's context passes one value for all. A wait without the upgrade: for a clone, the name is defined and the node still isn't an item.
- **Accepted cost:** a button is upgraded while out, as `createElement` does. By reading, a slotted element whose name is never defined stays in memory with its group until the page ends. `RF-69` declined that for a button on a page with no group, which is correct use, and an element that a page never defines in this group isn't.
- **Rows,** in core's `useRovingTabindex`, three engines: items cloned from a template, before the first connect and while out, one and all, with their `tabindex` after the connect and an arrow key; items defined after the host is connected; a removed item that is defined later gets no `tabindex`. In material-x, a connected group with cloned switch buttons, and one file that imports the switch button after the group, as `button-group-switch-order.browser.test.ts` does it the other way. **Witness:** each fails before the repair, except the removed item's. Without the upgrade the clones' fail, and without the wait the late definition's.
- **Read for the keys:** the third Tab in Firefox stays on the button for a group built by `innerHTML` and connected too, with and without the candidate ([probe](slot-listener-1/probes/keys.browser.test.ts.txt)). Its cause wasn't read, and it isn't this entry's.
- **Not read:** Safari, screen readers, sizes, a scoped registry, page-built users of `useRovingTabindex`.
- **Order:** after #256 (`RF-131`), because the group's rows read its slot while out. It doesn't wait for `RF-94` or `RF-130`.
- **Plan needed:** no. **Ready** for an implementer, on a branch of its own. Nothing is the owner's to answer.
- **Size:** _small_. One hook in core and its rows.

**Dated 2026-11-25 by the implementer: implemented on `core/roving-upgrade-1`, for #262, from `main` at `e57c9f074`, and not closed.** Requested by the coordinator. The direction holds in the three engines.

With the candidate's read in place of the hook's, five of the core rows fail in each engine, and none of material-x's.
