**The cause of the growth is the choice, and the property asked to reproduce it.** The hook keeps a tab stop that it chose only because an item was first, and so the result depends on the order in which items came. _"What it would be if the button had been an item at the slot change"_ makes a late definition rewrite that history, which takes a record of it. No user chose that tab stop, so nothing is owed to it.

**The contract now, in place of property 1's last sentence:**

- **The choice.** The tab stop is the enabled item that matches the group's value; or else the enabled item that focus moved it to last, while that item is in the slot; or else the first enabled item. Nothing else of the past counts. `focusin` still moves it at once.
- **A definition is read as a slot change is.** With the choice above, the same items then give the same tab stop, however late each was upgraded.
- **What changes for a group with no late button.** With no match and no focus, an item put first takes the tab stop, where the former one kept it. When the value stops matching, the tab stop goes to the item of the last focus or to the first one, where it stayed on the former match. Native radios with none checked are entered at the first one. The hook's JSDoc states the choice.
- **Accepted limit.** When focus has moved off the value's item and the value hasn't followed, a definition gives the tab stop back to the value's item, as each slot change does on `main`. Each difference that the fuzz shows in A to D and K is this one. So `reviewer-1`'s required property holds except where the value names the item. In G, 10 of the 29 differences are steps within one task and weren't classified.

| The candidate's plain second read, with the subject's two checks | +67 | 298, 715 | No |
| **The choice above, with that read** | **+76** | **0, 0** | **No** |

Bytes are of `connected-button-group` as the review reads them. The H and I numbers are against the items upgraded from the start with this choice, so I isn't comparable with the review's 239. The plain read is 9 B less. Its limit, that a late first button isn't the default, isn't taken, because the limit is the history again, and `RF-143` would carry it.

#### RF-142 — A disabled list item dims the focus indicator of the controls in it, which still work

Tier A, **open**, **ready** after #267 and #268 (the last note), pre-existing. Registered on 2026-11-25 by the architect, on `material-x/split-button-names-1`, from [#271](https://github.com/ausginer/material-x/issues/271), requested by the coordinator. It was seen by `RF-128`'s feature proof, on `material-x/handle-focus-1`. `RF-141` is the highest `RF-` on any branch on `origin`, so this is the next free number. Read at `c7db9e65a`, with `main` at `e57c9f074`, on the built elements, by Tab and from screenshots, in Playwright's Chromium 158, Firefox 159 and WebKit 27.2 ([reading](disabled-handle-1/checks/ring.txt), [probe](disabled-handle-1/probes/ring.mjs)).

- **The cause.** `:host(:state(disabled)) slot` in `interactive-box.styles.css` has the disabled opacity, 0.38. An opacity of the slot dims all that is painted in it, the outline of a control included.
- **What happens,** in `mx-list-button-item` and `mx-list-link-item` with `disabled`, in `lead`, in the three engines. The contrasts are of the indicator's darkest changed pixel with what was there before:

  | Control | Enabled item | Disabled item |
  | --- | --- | --- |
  | A handle, the browser's outline (today) | 14.6 to 18:1 in Chromium, 5:1 in Firefox, 2.7:1 in WebKit | 2.5:1, 1.8:1 and 1.4:1 |
  | A handle, `RF-128`'s outline | 5.6:1 | 1.8:1 |
  | `mx-icon-button`, its own indicator | 5.6:1 | 1.8:1 |
  | A native `<button>`, the browser's outline | 12:1, 5:1 and 2.6:1 | 2.3:1, 1.8:1 and 1.4:1 |

- **The controls work.** In the disabled item Tab reaches each of them, an arrow key on it proposes a move, and a click reaches it.
- **`trail`** has the same opacity. Its readings on `main` are of a clipped indicator (`RF-135`), so they aren't in the table.
- **Not affected:** a static `mx-list-item`, which can't be disabled, and an item's own indicator, which isn't in a slot.
- **Why it is a problem:** a keyboard user can't see where focus is, on a control that works. The exception for inactive components in the WCAG's contrast rule doesn't apply: the control is active.
- **Required property, until the last note,** for (a) or (b) below: the focus indicator of a control in a disabled item has the contrast that it has in an enabled one, in `lead` and `trail`, in the three engines, and the item's own content keeps its disabled look.
- **A candidate that holds for the handle, read in `lead`** ([reading](disabled-handle-1/checks/candidate.txt), [probe](disabled-handle-1/probes/candidate.mjs)): in `lead` and `trail` the opacity is on the slotted elements, `::slotted(:not(:focus-within))`, instead of on the slot. The focused handle's indicator is undimmed, 324 px of it in each engine, and the unfocused item has the same pixels with an icon and with a native button. **Its limits:** the focused control loses its dimming with its indicator, also after a click on it; an `mx-icon-button` is `display: contents`, so it takes no opacity and is drawn as enabled at all times; and, by reading, a page's own opacity on its element replaces the disabled one, and the trailing text's opacity isn't composed with it. The sizes weren't read.
- **Q1, for the owner — what does a disabled item do to the controls in it?**
  - **(a) The focused control, with its indicator, is drawn without the dimming. Recommended.** No behavior changes, and the item's disabled look changes only while a control in it has focus. With the candidate, an `mx-icon-button` is undimmed at all times, which is what it is: enabled. **Cost:** the limits above, and a few bytes in two bundles.
  - (b) A control in a disabled item is never dimmed, only the item's own text and icons. It is what the control is. The package can't tell a control from an icon or a text in a slot, apart from a handle and its own elements, so a page's native button would need a mark.
  - (c) A disabled item isn't reorderable: its handle isn't a button, takes no focus and lifts nothing. It changes the behavior that `RF-129`'s ruling reads, a page that only wants the item's action off loses its reorder, and other controls in the item stay dimmed.
  - (d) Nothing changes.
- **Order:** after #267 (`RF-128` with `RF-135`), whose `trail` and outline it reads, and after Q1.
- **Rows,** `browser`, in each engine, once Q1 is answered: for (a), the painted indicator of a handle and of an `mx-icon-button` in `lead` and in `trail` of a disabled button item has the computed color, with `coveredIndicator`, whose reading is nothing today. **Witness:** with the slot's opacity back, they fail. The unfocused disabled item has the opacity on its icon, its text and its label.
- **Not read:** `trail` without its clip, a slotted image or text, `selected` with `disabled`, forced colors, Safari, screen readers.
- **Plan needed:** no, once Q1 is answered. **Size:** _small_.

**Dated 2026-11-25 by the architect: Q1 is answered by the owner, (c), in a wider form, and it is `RD-61`.** Requested by the coordinator. **Read by the architect,** in Chromium, Firefox and WebKit, which agree in every row, with the sources of `main` at `56bba2895` ([reading](disabled-handle-1/checks/contract-before.txt), [probe](disabled-handle-1/probes/contract.browser.test.ts.txt)):

#### RF-143 — A member that can't take focus keeps a connected group's tab stop

Tier A, **open**, pre-existing. Registered on 2026-11-25 by the architect, on `core/hidden-1`, from `reviewer-1` of `RF-121`'s [feature proof](reviews/hidden-1/feature-proof-claude.md), requested by the coordinator. `RF-142` is the highest `RF-` on any branch on `origin`, so this is the next free number. No entry covers it: `RF-141` is about a member that isn't in the order. Read on the head of `RF-121`, built, in Playwright's Chromium, Firefox and WebKit, with the same result ([reading](hidden-1/checks/ruling.txt), [probe](hidden-1/probes/ruling.mjs)).

- **What happens,** in `mx-connected-button-group`, the only user of `useRovingTabindex`:
  - **The tab stop's member is hidden or disabled after the slot change:** Tab passes the whole group. `hidden` in the markup does the same. `disabled` there doesn't.
  - **Any member is hidden:** an arrow key that meets it goes no further. The tab stop moves to it and focus doesn't, so after that Tab passes the group too. A disabled member is skipped.
  - **The end member is hidden:** the first or last visible member has inner corners in place of the outer ones.
  - A page's `display: none` is as `hidden`, on the base also. `hidden` reaches this with `RF-121`, because before it a hidden member was shown.
- **The causes.** The hook excludes disabled items alone, and it chooses the tab stop at a slot change, a change of the group's value, a key and a `focusin`. No change of an item's own state is one of them. The group marks its ends by the slot's elements.
- **Why it is a problem:** a keyboard user can't reach visible, enabled controls. Disabling or hiding an option is ordinary use.
- **Required properties:**
  1. A member with `display: none` or `disabled` is never the tab stop and no key stops at it, whenever the hook chooses. `hidden` alone doesn't decide: a page's own `display` can show the member, and it is then one like the others.
  2. After a change of a member's `hidden` or `disabled`, the tab stop is chosen again, without a slot change. A tab stop that can still take focus stays, unless the group's value names another, so a first member that is shown again doesn't take it back.
  3. The same for a group that was built or changed while out, after its connect.
  4. The outer corners are on the first and the last member that isn't `display: none`, after the same changes.
  5. With no member that can take focus, there is no tab stop, as now.
- **Not required:** a change of a page's style alone, such as a media query, is heard at the next read. The arrow keys are right at once, by property 1. The tab stop isn't. The group's page says to hide a member with `hidden`.
- **It isn't the owner's.** An element that isn't rendered can't take focus in any engine, so skipping it is the one behavior that leaves the others reachable. Native radios do it: Tab reaches the first that is shown, in the three engines.
- **Direction, settled:** eligibility reads the computed `display` with `disabled`, and one `MutationObserver` for the hook hears both attributes. Read as a [candidate](hidden-1/probes/ruling-variants.mjs) on the head, for properties 1 and 2: each of its readings is right, except that Tab passes the group after a class hides its tab stop, which isn't required. The candidate doesn't read properties 3 and 4. While out, the computed `display` is empty, so property 3 needs a read at the connect. The group's ends can hear the same change or be CSS alone, the implementer's choice.
- **Not adopted.** `item.hidden` alone: wrong where a page shows the member, and it leaves the arrow keys stopped at a page's `display: none`. A `ResizeObserver`, for style changes too: the member's host is `display: contents` and has no size, and core doesn't know the member's shadow tree.
- **Relation to `RF-141` (#269).** Neither causes the other, and #269 waits for nothing here. Both change how the hook chooses, so this one is built on #269 merged, and `RF-141`'s rows pass unchanged. An upgraded item that is hidden isn't given the tab stop, and neither is a moved tab stop that can no longer take focus.
- **Rows,** three engines. In core: the tab stop's item hidden, disabled, and shown again; a hidden item in the arrow keys, Home and End; an item that a page's `display` shows; an item hidden in the markup; a group built while out; no eligible item. In material-x: Tab into a group whose first member is hidden, and disabled, and the corners with a hidden first and last member. **Witness:** each fails before the repair, except the page's `display` and no eligible item, which say what must not change. With `item.hidden` in place of the computed `display`, the page's `display` fails.
- **Not read:** Safari, screen readers, sizes, the group's own `disabled`, a member hidden or disabled while it has focus, and the standard group's `:first-child` and `:last-child` with a hidden member.
- **Plan needed:** no. **Ready** for an implementer, after #269 and #270, on a branch of its own. Nothing is the owner's to answer.
- **Size:** _medium_. One hook in core, the connected group, its page and their rows.

**Dated 2026-11-25 by the implementer: implemented on `core/roving-hidden-1`, for #273, from `main` at `2485fb2df`, and not closed.** Requested by the coordinator. It is built on `RF-141`'s choice, whose last note replaces this entry's property 2's sentence about a first member that is shown again.

- **The hook:** eligibility is `disabled` and the computed `display`, one `MutationObserver` hears the items' `hidden` and `disabled`, and the tab stop is chosen again at the connect. The observer is on each item of the last read, because a wider one would also choose again for a change inside an item or of the host's own `disabled`.
- **The group:** its ends are marked by the computed `display`, at a slot change, at the connect, and after a change of `hidden`.
- **One rule more than the direction names:** a member that is the only one shown is both ends. The former sheet gave it the last member's corners, so `::slotted([data-first][data-last])` has the outer corner on all sides. Property 4 asks for it. A group with one member had the same corners before.
- **Engines: Chromium, on the owner's ruling of 2026-11-25,** relayed by the coordinator, that development runs in Chromium and the review in the three engines. It came while the witnesses ran. Finished before it: the rows in the three engines, the witnesses in Chromium and Firefox, and in WebKit the first five mutations. The WebKit run was ended, and the sources and core's build are restored.
- **Rows:** 30 in core's `useRovingTabindex` (95 in all), three in `button-group.browser.test.ts` and seven in `button-group.spec.browser.test.ts`. They pass in Chromium, Firefox and WebKit. **Witnesses,** Chromium ([reading](roving-hidden-1/checks/witnesses.txt), [probe](roving-hidden-1/probes/mutate.mjs)):

**Dated 2026-11-26 by the architect: the [feature proof](reviews/roving-hidden-1/feature-proof-claude.md) of `810cffceb` is ruled, and properties 1 and 4 are amended,** requested by the coordinator. The three findings are accepted. My own reading is of the end marks by CSS alone, in the three engines one at a time ([reading](roving-hidden-1/checks/ruling-ends.txt), [probe](roving-hidden-1/probes/ruling-ends.mjs), [again after frames](roving-hidden-1/probes/ruling-ends-frames.mjs)). The rest is the proof's readings.

**One cause behind two findings: the computed `display` is read where an attribute already decides.** WebKit keeps a stale `display` in a subtree that isn't rendered (`reviewer-1`), and an undefined member that a page hides has `display: none` with no change to hear when it is defined (`reviewer-2`). The group's reads of computed style, between its writes of the marks, are the cost (`reviewer-3`), by the proof's attribution. Where the page used `hidden`, the attribute gives the right answer in each case without a read.

**The contract now:**

- **Property 1, in place of its second sentence** (_"`hidden` alone doesn't decide: a page's own `display` can show the member, and it is then one like the others"_): **a member with the `hidden` attribute is out, whatever a page's style does with it.** The computed `display` still decides for a member without `hidden`, so a page's own `display: none` still keeps the keys from it. A page that shows a hidden member has a member that the keys don't reach. The author declared it irrelevant, and the group's page says to hide a member with `hidden`. Keeping the computed `display` as the only test leaves the unit's own finding open in WebKit, for correct use, in an inactive panel.
- **Property 4, in place of its first sentence:** the outer corners are on the first and the last member **without the `hidden` attribute**, after a slot change or a change of a member's `hidden`. The ends read no computed style, so they need no read at the connect. A member that a page's style alone hides or shows doesn't move the corners. That is visual only, because the tab stop and the keys follow property 1.
- **Not adopted: ends by CSS alone,** `::slotted(:nth-child(1 of :not([hidden])))` and its `:nth-last-child` twin. They match in the three engines when the group is built, also in RTL and with undefined members. In WebKit, a change of a sibling's `hidden` isn't matched again, also two frames later, so every end stays unmarked until something else changes the group.
- **Not adopted: the group's reads kept, written only where a mark changes.** It would keep a page's style for the corners, which the ends don't need. `reviewer-2` would still need the group to hear a definition, which only the hook hears, and `reviewer-1`'s corners would stay stale in WebKit.

**Triage:**

- **`reviewer-1`: accepted, pre-existing.** Answered by property 1 as amended: the observer hears `hidden`, and the attribute isn't stale. **The limit that stays, WebKit's, accepted:** a member that is shown again while its group isn't rendered still reads `display: none` there. It isn't given the tab stop back at that change, and the next choice gives it. Another member keeps the tab stop meanwhile, so Tab still enters the group, on another member than the value's when the value names it. The entry and the hook's JSDoc say nothing of it, as of any engine's defect, and this note records it.
- **`reviewer-2`: accepted, this unit's regression.** Answered by property 4 as amended: an undefined member that a page hides has no `hidden`, so it is an end before and after its definition.
- **`reviewer-3`: accepted, this unit's. A group without a hidden member may not cost this:** each `mx-split-button` has one, and its members are never hidden. With the group's ends of `main` and this unit's hook, the proof reads `main`'s times in Chromium, so the hook's reads at the connect are accepted. **Required property:** in Chromium, connecting 20, 100 and 300 groups of four, and as many split buttons, in one task, each median of seven is at most 1.5 times `main`'s, read in turn with `main`, three times. It is a reading, not a row, because a row can't hold a time on a loaded machine.
- **The departure, the only shown member with four outer corners, and a group of one with them too:** accepted, as the proof accepts it.
- **It isn't the owner's.** The changes are of a unit that isn't on `main`, and core has no release. A page that shows a hidden member is the only one that sees a difference, and its own markup contradicts itself there.

**The list:**

1. **The hook:** an item with the `hidden` attribute isn't eligible. The computed `display` is read only for an item that is enabled and not hidden. The hook's JSDoc and the comment on `eligible` state property 1 as amended.
2. **The group:** the ends are marked by `hidden` at a slot change and at a change of a member's `hidden`. The read at the connect and the reads of computed style go. A mark is written only where it changes, so a slot change that changes no end writes nothing. That is how to write it, not a required property. The group's JSDoc already says _"isn't hidden"_.
3. **`connected-button-group.mdx`,** the sentence after _"Hide a member with its `hidden` attribute."_: a hidden member stays out of the group's order even where a page's style shows it. When a style alone hides or shows a member, the tab stop follows at the group's next change, and the outer corners don't follow it.
4. **Rows that change:** core's two rows _"hidden and shown by a page's display"_ now say that a hidden item that a page's `display` shows isn't the tab stop, and that an arrow key passes it. material-x's _"should count a hidden member that a page's display shows"_ now says that the ends pass over it. Core's row _"should skip an item on an arrow key that a style alone hides"_ stays.
5. **Rows added:**
   - In core: an item hidden while the host's ancestor has `hidden` isn't the tab stop, and the next item is, after the ancestor is shown. The same with `hidden` on the host.
   - In material-x: a group in a `hidden` ancestor, its first member hidden, then the ancestor shown: Tab reaches the second member, and the ends are on the second and the last.
   - In material-x: a page with `:not(:defined) { display: none }`, the group defined before its members: after their definition, the ends are on the first and the last.
6. **Witnesses:** `hidden` not read by the hook, which fails the core and material-x rows of the hidden ancestor in WebKit, and core's rows of item 4 in each engine; the group's ends by the computed `display`, as at `810cffceb`, which fails the `:not(:defined)` row in Chromium and the material-x row of item 4; the ends not marked at a change of `hidden`. The rows of the hidden ancestor are blind in Chromium, which reads `none` there. They are witnessed in WebKit, under `RD-62`, in those two files only.
7. **The cost reading** of `reviewer-3` in Chromium, with the proof's [probe](reviews/roving-hidden-1/probes/proof-cost.browser.test.ts.txt), recorded with the unit.

**Checks owed:** the affected rows in Chromium, the witnesses there and in WebKit as item 6 says, the size table, typecheck, lint and the root format check.

**Recheck:** targeted, by the same reviewer, in the three engines: the proof's readings of the group while it isn't rendered and of a late definition, the cost in turn with `main` in each engine, the sizes, and the new witnesses. Nothing else of the proof is read again.

#### RF-144 — A control in a slot of `mx-list-button-item` or `mx-list-link-item` is inside the item's button or link

Tier A, **open**, pre-existing. Registered on 2026-11-25 by the architect, on `repo/axe-checks-1`, from the readings of `RD-57`'s plan. `RF-143` is the highest `RF-` on any branch on `origin` (`core/hidden-1`), so this is the next free number. Read at `8bed561de` in Chromium, Firefox and WebKit ([readings](axe-checks-1/checks/nested.txt), [probe](axe-checks-1/probes/nested.browser.test.ts.txt)).

- **What happens:** the item's slots are inside its `<button>` or `<a>`. A focusable control in a slot, a sortable handle, an `mx-icon-button` or a native button, is then inside the item's control. axe-core 4.14.1 reports `nested-interactive` on the button item, in the three engines, and nothing on the link item. In Chromium's tree the nested control is exposed inside the item's button or link, and the item's name takes the control's: `Move A A`, `A More`.
- **Why it is a problem:** `list.mdx` says that a `trail` slot takes a control, _the same in the three items_, and that a `data-handle` child is an item's handle. So a page that follows it meets this. HTML doesn't allow interactive content in a `<button>` or an `<a>`, and a button's descendants are presentational to some assistive technology.
- **Not a problem:** an `mx-list-item`, whose controls are beside its content, and an `mx-list-item` with a handle.
- **Required property:** a control in a slot of an interactive item has its own place in the accessibility tree, outside the item's button or link, and doesn't change the item's name; or the documentation says which slots and which elements are supported. Which of the two is the plan's to say.
- **Not established:** the trees of Firefox and WebKit, and what a screen reader announces.
- **Interaction:** `RD-57`'s list names the button item's lines, and a repair removes them. `RF-142` doesn't touch it.
- **Plan needed:** yes, by the architect. It changes the items' structure.
- **Size:** _large_.

#### RF-145 — In Chromium, touch doesn't reorder an item by most handles, `mx-icon` among them

Tier A, **open**, **ready**, pre-existing. Registered on 2026-11-25 by the architect, on `material-x/disabled-item-1`, from an observation of #278's feature proof, requested by the coordinator. `RF-144` is the highest `RF-` on any branch on `origin` (`repo/axe-checks-1`), so this is the next free number. Read in Chromium 158 by CDP touch, on the built elements of `754e2089f`, an enabled item, static and button, in `lead` and `trail` ([reading](inline-handle-1/checks/touch.txt), [probe](inline-handle-1/probes/touch.mjs)), and without the package ([reading](inline-handle-1/checks/slot-text.txt), [probe](inline-handle-1/probes/slot-text.mjs)). `main` wasn't run; its `touch-action` line is the same.

- **What happens:** the item is lifted, and then the finger pans: the browser sends `pointercancel`, which ends the drag. The handle has `touch-action: none` in its inline style in each case.

  | Handle                                          | Touch    |
  | ----------------------------------------------- | -------- |
  | `mx-icon`, the handle of the list's own stories | Canceled |
  | A `span` with text or with an `mx-icon`         | Canceled |
  | `mx-icon-button`                                | Canceled |
  | A native button with an `mx-icon`               | Canceled |
  | A native button with text                       | Works    |

- **Two causes.** `touch-action` doesn't apply to an inline element, nor to a `display: contents` one, which `mx-icon-button`'s host is. And in Chromium, a text slotted into a `display: contents` slot doesn't have the touch action of the host around it: with no package code, a host with `touch-action: none` and a `<slot>` pans from its text, and with a `span` or `div` around the slot too. With `slot { display: block }`, or with an element as the slotted content, it doesn't. The text of `mx-icon` is slotted so.
- **Why it is a problem:** the JSDoc promises `touch-action: none` for any `[data-handle]` child, and the documented handle is an icon. In Chromium, a touch user can't reorder by it.
- **Required properties:**
  1. A touch that starts on a handle of an enabled item, the handle an inline element, an `mx-icon`, an `mx-icon-button` or a native button with any of them in it, lifts the item and isn't canceled by a pan.
  2. Nothing changes for a mouse, the keyboard, a disabled item (`RD-61` property 2) or a page's own `touch-action`, which stands.
- **Candidate, read in Chromium:** `display: inline-block` on a slotted `[data-handle]`, and `display: block` on `mx-icon`'s slot. Either alone leaves some of the table canceled, and both together pass all of it. Each changes boxes: the span handle in `lead` was 9x17 and is 9x0 in the reading, and a page's `display` on the handle must still win. Where the rules go is the implementer's.
- **Interaction:** `RF-137` (`material-x/icon-name-1`) puts `mx-icon`'s slot in a `<span aria-hidden="true">`, which fails in the reading without the package as the plain slot does. So the repair must hold on both, and the second to land reads the other.
- **Rows,** `browser`, in Chromium, by CDP touch: property 1 for each handle. **Witness:** each fails at `754e2089f`. Screenshots of the handles' boxes don't change, or the owner sees them.
- **Not read:** Firefox, beyond the owner's check below, WebKit and Safari, and whether the package's other touch surfaces meet the same.
- **Size:** _medium_.

**Dated 2026-11-25 by the architect: confirmed by the owner on a phone, in Chrome on Android with real touch,** the same day, relayed by the coordinator (the phone and the versions aren't known, nor which handle he tried). His words: _"Ручка: не тащится. Происходит покрас, начинается движение - и тут же сбрасывается"_ ("The handle: it doesn't drag. It is painted, the move starts, and is at once reset"). It is what the emulation shows: a lift, and then a `pointercancel`. Properties, order and size don't change. An item without a handle is `RF-146`.

**Dated 2026-11-25 by the architect: this unit also carries `RF-146`'s (a),** the documentation of an item without a handle and one row, as that entry's last note says. Nothing else of this entry changes.

**Added the same day: Firefox on the same phone,** relayed by the coordinator: _"работает, но «схватиться» за ручку сложнее, чем в хроме"_ ("it works, but it is harder to grab the handle than in Chrome"). It is the handle only: an item without one doesn't move there either (`RF-146`). That it works fits the second cause, which is read in Chromium only, if the handle was the stories' `mx-icon`: that host is `inline-block`, so the first cause doesn't apply to it. **Why it is harder isn't established.** The touch target is small: `mx-icon` in `lead` and in `trail` is 20x20 px in the [reading](inline-handle-1/checks/touch.txt), below the 24x24 of WCAG 2.5.8 without its spacing exception and the 48 dp that Material asks for (both by knowledge, not read here). It is the same in both browsers, so alone it explains that a handle is hard to grab and not the difference. A difference in how each browser moves a touch to a nearby target could, and wasn't read. A larger target isn't a property of this entry: it changes the look or the hit area of every handle, and gets an entry of its own if the owner wants it.

**Dated 2026-11-26 by the implementer: implemented on `material-x/touch-handle-1`, from `main` at `d20c47bda`, with `RF-146`'s (a), and the entry isn't closed.** Requested by the coordinator.

- **Code:** the candidate, placed so. In the item's styles (`list/styles/item/main.styles.css`), beside the handle's focus rule: `:is(.lead, .trail)::slotted([data-handle])` is `display: inline-block`, except with `hidden` other than `until-found`, as the avatar's rule does. A `::slotted` rule loses to a page's own rule, so a page's `display` wins. In `mx-icon`'s styles, `slot { display: inline }`, not `block`: any box on the slot ends the pan in Chromium, `inline` and `block` alike, with or without `aria-hidden` on the slot ([reading](touch-handle-1/checks/slot-display.txt), [probe](touch-handle-1/probes/slot-display.mjs)). `inline` changes no box of `mx-icon`, and it is the rule that `RF-137` adds for WebKit.

Both readings above with `aria-hidden` on the inline slot pass. So the second to land keeps one rule and both comments, a text conflict and nothing else. The second's rows, run on the merged tree, are what confirms it.
- **Rows,** in `sortable-list.browser`, Chromium only (`describe.runIf`), by CDP touch: a touch drag by each handle of property 1 (a `span` with text, an `mx-icon`, a `span` with an `mx-icon`, an `mx-icon-button`, a native button with an `mx-icon`), in `lead` and in `trail`, proposes the move: 10 rows. In every engine: a page's `display` on a handle stands, and a hidden handle stays hidden: 2 rows. `RF-146`'s row is in that entry.
- **Witnesses,** Chromium: with the two CSS files at `d20c47bda`, the 10 touch rows fail and the others pass ([reading](touch-handle-1/checks/witness-main.txt)). One mutation at a time ([reading](touch-handle-1/checks/mutations.txt)): without the handle rule, the 6 rows of a `span` and an `mx-icon-button` fail; with a `display: contents` slot, the 6 of an `mx-icon` alone, in a `span` or in a button fail; without the `hidden` guard, the hidden row fails; with `!important`, the page's `display` row fails.
- **Boxes** ([reading](touch-handle-1/checks/boxes.txt), [probes](touch-handle-1/probes/boxes.mjs)), at rest and with the handle focused, in a static and a button item, in `lead` and `trail`, and `mx-icon` alone and in `mx-button`, `mx-icon-button` and `mx-fab`. **At rest, no screenshot changes.** `mx-icon` as the handle, as the stories have it, and a native button, change nothing focused either. **What changes, for the owner:** the box of a `span` handle, and so its focus indicator. The `lead` slot has `line-height: 0`, so a `span` with text there goes from 9x17 to 9x0, and its indicator closes onto the glyph ([before and after](touch-handle-1/checks/boxes/lead-span-text-focus.png)). In `trail`, a `span` grows from 12 to 16 high ([before and after](touch-handle-1/checks/boxes/trail-span-mx-icon-focus.png)), and a `span` with an `mx-icon` in `lead` goes from 16x17 to 16x16. The `mx-icon-button` host is `inline-block` instead of `display: contents`, with the same 40x40 box. In a button item, two runs of the same tree differ in the focused screenshots by up to 118 pixels, so that variant isn't read there. A remedy for the `span` in `lead`, such as a `line-height` on the handle, isn't read and isn't decided.
- **Size, Brotli** ([sizes](touch-handle-1/checks/sizes.txt)): `icon/icon` 667 to 673, `list/list-item` 2803 to 2816, `complete` 25988 to 26034. `list/sortable-list` doesn't move. No row has a limit.
- **Checks,** Chromium: the `browser` project (1259 rows) and the `spec` project (796, 2 expected failures), and the typecheck. **Not run:** Firefox and WebKit, the visual project, the docs build.

**Dated 2026-11-26 by the architect: the feature proof's three observations.** Requested by the coordinator. Read: the [feature proof](reviews/touch-handle-1/feature-proof-claude.md) of `df577d7df`, which accepts with no finding, and the diff of `ebb8a3a92` from `d20c47bda`. Nothing was probed again. No property changes, and nothing is the owner's but the boxes below.

- **1, the handle rule in a plain `mx-list`: nothing is owed.** The rule stays in the item's styles, beside the handle's focus rule, which already applies in any list. To apply only in the sortable list, the item would need a state that the list sets on each item, which is code in every item for a box that `data-handle` gives no meaning to outside that list. In a plain list the list makes no handle focusable, and at rest the changed box draws nothing different. The texts state the box for the sortable list, which is the one documented use.
- **2, the sizes: nothing is owed.** The [reading](touch-handle-1/checks/sizes.txt) names the nine rows that move, and none has a limit. The implementer's note above names three. The other six: `button/split-button` +11, `checkbox/checkbox` +8, `radio/radio` +11, `text-field/text-field` +17, `list/list-link-item` +18 and `list/list-button-item` −14 B, Brotli.
- **3, `hidden="until-found"`: one row is owed.** The rule now hides an `until-found` handle's content until it is found, as HTML defines that state. On `main`, an inline `span` with it drew its text, because `content-visibility` doesn't apply to an inline box. The handle's guard is the one that `.host` and the avatar's rule use, and `tests/core/hidden.browser.test.ts` has rows for `.host`'s. #### RF-146 — By touch, an item without a handle isn't reordered

Tier A, **open**, **ready, with `RF-145`'s unit** (the last note), pre-existing. Until that note: waiting on the owner (Q1). Registered on 2026-11-25 by the architect, on `material-x/disabled-item-1`, from the same check by the owner, relayed by the coordinator: _"Без ручки: вообще ничего не происходит, браузер пытается текст выделить вместо перетаскивания"_ ("Without a handle: nothing happens at all, the browser tries to select text instead of dragging"). Read in Chromium 158, by CDP touch, on the built elements of `754e2089f` ([reading](inline-handle-1/checks/no-handle.txt), [probe](inline-handle-1/probes/no-handle.mjs)).

- **What happens, emulated:** on a static, a button and a link item the finger's move lifts the item, the pan sends `pointercancel`, and nothing is proposed. A press held for 800 ms before the move gives the same. With `touch-action: none` on the item each of them is proposed. The mouse works throughout. Emulation never selected text, which the phone does, and the phone shows no lift.
- **On the phone, the same in Firefox and in Chrome on Android,** by the owner, relayed by the coordinator on the same day: in Firefox only text is selected, and nothing moves.
- **What is promised:** `list.mdx` and the JSDoc say that an item without a handle drags _by its whole surface_, and that the user reorders _by pointer_. Neither names touch. drag leaves it to its consumer: _"Give each row `touch-action: none` for touch input and `user-select: none` for text"_, and has no long press. `mx-sortable-list` is that consumer and writes `touch-action` on handles only. `RD-31` (Q3, Q6) decided the whole-surface drag, and no record decided what a finger does there, where a swipe is also how the page scrolls.
- **So it isn't by contract, and it isn't `RF-145`:** that is a handle that has `touch-action: none` and loses it. Here nothing asks for it, and the repair is a choice.
- **Q1, for the owner — what does a finger do on an item without a handle?**
  - **(a) It scrolls, as on any item. A touch user reorders by a handle. Recommended for now.** The documentation says that an item without a handle is reordered by mouse, pen where it doesn't scroll, and keyboard, and that a list used by touch gives its items handles. No code. **Cost:** such a list can't be reordered by touch.
  - (b) It drags at once: the item has `touch-action: none` and `user-select: none`. A few lines. **Cost:** a finger on an item can't scroll the page or the list, so a list longer than the screen can't be scrolled by its items.
  - (c) A press held for a moment lifts the item, and a swipe scrolls. It is the usual pattern on phones. **Cost:** drag has to change, which has no long press today: a delay before the activation for touch, a non-passive listener that keeps the browser from scrolling after the lift, and the selection and the menu of a long press suppressed. Not measured or planned. It can follow (a) later.
- **Why (a):** it keeps scrolling, which everybody needs, and breaks nothing. (b) trades a broken scroll for a drag. (c) is the right behavior if touch matters for these lists, and is a feature with its own decision in drag, so it needs his word.
- **After the answer:** (a) is the JSDoc and `list.mdx`, _small_. (b) is _small_, with rows by CDP touch. (c) is _large_, with a plan first, in drag and then here.
- **Order:** it waits for no unit, and `RF-145` doesn't wait for it.
- **Not read:** Firefox beyond the owner's check, WebKit and Safari, the phone's long press beyond the owner's words, and what Material says.

**Dated 2026-11-25 by the architect: the owner answered Q1 with (a), and wants (c) later.** In chat, relayed by the coordinator: _"Согласен с тобой: (а) сейчас, (с) на потом"_ ("I agree with you: (a) now, (c) for later"). The coordinator had proposed that (c) gets an entry of its own, which is `RQ-3`. He took up no larger handle target (`RF-145`'s last note), so it has no entry. `RD-31` property 4 has the rule.

- **Where: `RF-145`'s unit,** on its branch and in its pull request, which closes both. The text sends a touch user to a handle, and in Chromium most handles don't work by touch until that repair. So (a) doesn't land before it, and isn't added to #278, whose proof is done. Both are ready to be taken, on the base that has #278, which changes the same documents.
- **Required properties:**
  1. Each place in the table says what it says now, and that: a mouse drags an item without a handle by its whole surface, and so does a pen where the browser doesn't scroll with it; a finger on it doesn't reorder it and does what it does on any item, such as scroll; and the items of a list that is used by touch need handles.
  2. No text promises a touch reorder of an item without a handle.
  3. No code changes for (a). `touch-action` and `user-select` aren't written on an item.

#### RF-147 — An `mx-icon` inline in a page's text stands on the text's baseline, off its center

Tier C, **open**, **ready** (the last note), pre-existing. Registered on 2026-11-26 by the architect, on `repo/axe-checks-1`, from #299, which the owner asked to register, relayed by the coordinator. The observation is `RF-145`'s note of 2026-11-26 on the focused handles (`material-x/touch-handle-1`, #296). `RF-146` is the highest `RF-` on any branch on `origin`, so this is the next free number.

- **What happens:** `mx-icon`'s host is `display: inline-block` with `overflow: hidden` (`icon.ctr.css`), so by CSS its baseline is its bottom margin edge. Inline in a line of text, its bottom stands on the text's baseline, and the space of the text's descenders is below it: the icon sits higher than the text around it. Read in Chromium on #296's branch, `material-x/touch-handle-1`, in its `.plan/touch-handle-1/checks/remedy-boxes.txt`, which merges with it: in a `span` of 11 px text with a 16 px line, an 11 px icon has 0 px above it and 5 below. In a native button with its own text styles, a 13 px icon has 3 above and 6 below, on `main` too.
- **Where it shows:** wherever a page puts an `mx-icon` in its own text or in an inline element of its own. **Where it doesn't:** in the package's own elements, where the icon is a flex or grid item, which `vertical-align` doesn't move: `RF-145`'s boxes reading has `mx-button`, `mx-icon-button` and `mx-fab` unchanged. A sortable handle centers its content by `RF-145`'s remedy.
- **Why it is a problem:** an icon beside text looks misplaced, by up to its text's descender. The owner has fought it often, in his words. No Material token states where an inline icon stands.
- **Required property:** an `mx-icon` inline in a line of text, at its text's size, stands where Q1 says, within 1 px at 24 px, in each engine at `RD-20`'s floor. The boxes of `mx-icon` in the package's own elements don't change, and no visual baseline changes.
- **Q1, for the owner — where does an inline icon stand?**
  - **(a) Its middle on the middle of the text's lowercase letters,** CSS's `vertical-align: middle`. Defined by the font's x-height, so the same rule in every font. **Recommended,** because it needs no number of its own.
  - **(b) Its middle on the middle of the text's line,** which suits text in capitals and numerals. A fixed offset, such as `-0.125em`, comes near it for most fonts, and only near.
  - **(c) As today,** on the baseline, with a sentence in `icon.mdx` that says so and how a page moves it.
- **Candidates, not read:** a `vertical-align` on the host for (a) or (b); `overflow: visible`, which would put the baseline at the glyph's own, and changes what a large glyph may paint outside its box.
- **Rows,** the three engines: an icon inline in text, at the text's size, at two sizes, measured against the text's box as Q1 defines it. **Witness:** each fails on `main`. The boxes of `RF-145`'s reading for the package's elements are unchanged.
- **Not read:** Safari, a page's own font, an icon with a size other than its text's, an SVG in `mx-icon`.
- **Plan needed:** no, once Q1 is answered. **Size:** _small_.

**Dated 2026-11-26 by the architect: Q1 is answered by the owner, (a),** relayed by the coordinator: _"(a)"_. An inline icon's middle stands on the middle of its text's lowercase letters. **Ready** for an implementer, in a unit of its own, on a branch from `main` after #293 merges, because this entry is on #293's branch until then and the subject isn't that unit's. The status above said _"waiting on the owner (Q1)"_. The size stays _small_.

- **The property, made exact:** in each engine at `RD-20`'s floor, the vertical middle of an `mx-icon` inline in a line of text is within 1 px of the text's baseline plus half its x-height, at 16 and 24 px. The x-height is measured independently of CSS's `middle`, for example by a canvas `measureText('x')` in the text's font, so the row doesn't assert the rule with itself.
- **The candidate, and its form is the implementer's:** `vertical-align: middle` on the host in `icon.ctr.css`, with a comment that gives the reason: an `inline-block` with `overflow: hidden` stands on its bottom edge.
- **Rows,** the three engines: the property at both sizes, in a `span` of text and in a native button with text. **Witness:** each fails on `main`.
- **Unchanged, and read:** the boxes of `mx-icon` in `mx-button`, `mx-icon-button`, `mx-fab`, a list item's `lead` and `trail`, and a sortable handle, with `RF-145`'s probe (`material-x/touch-handle-1`'s `.plan/touch-handle-1/probes/boxes.mjs`, or a copy). In a slot whose line is 0 high, the icon's place shouldn't move, and the reading says whether it does.
- **Visual baselines:** none is to change but where an icon stands in a line of text, such as the icon's own stories. Each one that changes is recorded by `RD-13` and shown to the owner before and after.
- **Stop** and return if an element of the package moves, or the property doesn't hold in an engine.
- **Feature proof:** owed, in the three engines.

**Dated 2026-11-26 by the implementer: (a) is implemented on `material-x/icon-middle-1`, and the unit stops at its _Stop_ line, for one reading.** From `main` at `e457ed209`, in Chromium (`RD-62`). The record is `.plan/icon-middle-1/`.

- **The change:** `vertical-align: middle` on the host in `icon.ctr.css`, with the comment the candidate asks for.
- **Rows,** in `tests/icon/icon.browser.test.ts`, at 16 and 24 px: an icon in a `span` of text and in a native button with text, measured against the baseline of an empty `inline-block` and the x-height that a canvas reads. #### RF-148 — A button's label that wraps is drawn outside the button, which keeps its height

Tier A, **open**, **ruling owed** (Q1), pre-existing. Registered on 2026-11-26 by the architect, on `repo/register-observations-9`, from [#294](https://github.com/ausginer/material-x/issues/294), requested by the coordinator. The observation is `RF-139`'s note of 2026-11-26 on #286's feature proof, which left it to `mx-button`. `RF-147` is the highest `RF-` on any branch on `origin`, so this is the next free number. The source is read at `e457ed209`. The measurements are #286's, in Chromium: the first on its candidate `keep`, which it implemented, and the second at its recheck.

- **What happens:** when a button is narrower than its label, the label wraps between its words, and the button stays 40 px high. The lines are drawn above and below its box, over what is beside it. In Chromium, in a 240 px list item beside a video, _A button of several words_ is a 79.7 × 40 px button with five lines, in an item 80 px high ([reading](item-overflow-1/checks/words-chromium.txt), line 34). With `overflow-wrap: anywhere` through `::part(impl)`, _Download_ in a 60 px container has three lines, 56 px high, in a 60 × 40 px button ([reading](reviews/item-overflow-1/checks/recheck-outside-chromium.txt)).
- **The cause, by reading:** `.host` in `button/styles/default/main.styles.css` has `max-block-size: var(--_container-height)` and a block padding computed for one line, and nothing that keeps the label on one line or clips it. The sheet is the one that `ButtonCore` adopts, so `mx-button`, `mx-link-button`, `mx-switch-button` and the split button's leading button have it.
- **Since `RF-139`'s ruling,** the label breaks only between its words, unless a page breaks it through `::part(impl)`. A label of one word then stays on one line and the button runs out of a narrow container instead. A label of several words still wraps.
- **Why it is a problem:** the lines cover the content beside and below the button, such as the next list item, and the button's shape, its state layer and its focus indicator don't enclose its label.
- **Required property:** in any container, every line of a button's label is inside the button's box, in each engine at `RD-20`'s floor. Which way is Q1's.
- **Q1, for the architect, or the owner if it changes what a page may expect — what does a button do with a label that doesn't fit?**
  - **(a) It keeps one line,** and the button is as wide as its label. A narrow container gets a button that runs out of it, as a one-word label does today.
  - **(b) It grows** to its lines' height, with the same padding. The button's height then depends on its container.
  - **(c) It keeps one line and truncates** the label with an ellipsis. Its words are lost, and the accessible name keeps them.
  - **No recommendation yet:** whether Material lets a button's label wrap, or truncate, wasn't read. Its answer decides between (a), (b) and (c).
- **Rows,** the three engines, on `mx-button`, `mx-link-button` and `mx-switch-button`: a label of several words in a container narrower than it, and with `overflow-wrap: anywhere` through `::part(impl)`. Every line of the label is inside the button's box. **Witness:** each fails on `main`. `RF-139`'s rows in `tests/button/button-label-breaks.browser.test.ts` and the list's rows keep passing, or change as Q1 says.
- **Not read:** Material's guidance, Firefox, WebKit, Safari, the icon button's and the FAB's labels (the extended FAB's is `nowrap`), visual baselines.
- **Plan needed:** no, once Q1 is answered. **Size:** _small_ after Q1.

#### RF-151 — In WebKit, a mouse drag of a list item highlights its text

Tier A, **closed 2026-11-26** by #314 at `a36f577f8` (the last note). Before closure: open, ready, not this unit's. Registered on 2026-11-26 by the architect, on `material-x/sortable-displacement-1`, from the implementer's side observation in `RD-60`'s unit, relayed by the coordinator. `RF-150` is the entry before this one. Read at `5448c4fd6`, on one screenshot.

- **What was observed:** the unit's probe lifts `B` of an `mx-sortable-list` of four `mx-list-item`s without handles, with `commands.pointerPress` and two `pointerMove`s, and screenshots the list while the item is held over `C`. In WebKit, the text _"xt"_ of the lifted item is highlighted under the pointer ([screenshot](sortable-displacement-1/checks/shots/webkit-overshoot-pointer.png), [probe](sortable-displacement-1/probes/shots.browser.test.ts.txt), _"overshoot, pointer drop"_). In Chromium and Firefox, the same frame has no highlight.
- **What drag does:** its kernel clears the selection when a drag activates (`packages/drag/src/kernel/session.ts`, `#move`). It never prevents a press, and `draggable`'s JSDoc tells the consumer to give the handle `user-select: none` for text. An item without a handle is its own handle, and `mx-sortable-list` writes no `user-select` on it. `RF-146` property 3 decided that, for touch. So WebKit extends a selection after the activation, as the mouse moves.
- **Why it is a problem:** the user sees a text selection on the item they are moving, which no other engine shows and nothing in the list's documentation promises.
- **Not this unit's,** by reading: `RD-60`'s unit changes no input, selection or `user-select` code. **Not read at the base.**
- **Required property:** in each engine, while a mouse drags an item without a handle, and after its drop, no text of the list is selected. A press without a drag still selects text as it does today, unless the repair decides otherwise and says so. **Witness:** a row in `browser`, in each engine, by real mouse input, that reads the document's selection during the drag and after the drop, and fails in WebKit at `5448c4fd6`.
- **For the unit that takes it:** the repair amends `RF-146` property 3 if it writes `user-select` on an item. Whether WebKit reports this highlight through `getSelection()` decides whether the row can read it, or needs a screenshot.
- **Not read:** Safari, an item with a handle, the button and link items, the selection after the drop, whether `getSelection()` reports the highlight.
- **Plan needed:** no. **Size:** _small_.

**Dated 2026-11-26 by the architect: the repair is on the list, by `user-select` on an item in a drag, and drag's kernel doesn't change,** on `material-x/drag-selection-1`, requested by the coordinator, read at `d6f6cf60b`. The implementer offered two repairs. (A) prevents each `pointermove` of an active drag in drag's kernel. (B) writes `user-select: none` on an item that is in a drag. The implementer's reading is that WebKit reports the highlight through `getSelection()`: the press's selection grows with each move after the kernel's `removeAllRanges` at the activation, and it stays after a drop that the page doesn't commit.

- **(B) is chosen.** drag's contract already assigns text to the consumer. Its README and `draggable`'s JSDoc say to give the handle `user-select: none` for text, and `mx-sortable-list` is the consumer that didn't. (A) would change `drag:DRI-11`, _"Only the move that crosses the threshold is prevented"_, a guarantee to every consumer of drag, to repair one consumer. That needs the owner's word, and nothing here needs it.
- **(B) covers more than the item, by reading:** in WebKit, with the press in the lifted item's text, a held pointer that leaves the list over a page paragraph selects nothing, during the drag and after the drop. Without (B) it selects `e text` ([reading](drag-selection-1/checks/off-list.txt), [probe](drag-selection-1/probes/off-list.browser.test.ts.txt)). Chromium selects nothing either way. The implementer's three rows pass with (B) in WebKit and Chromium.
- **`RF-146` property 3 is amended,** in its own note: `user-select` is written on an item only while the item is in a drag.
- **Required properties:**
  1. An item in a pointer drag isn't selectable, nor is its content, whatever its kind: `mx-list-item`, `mx-list-button-item` and `mx-list-link-item`. One rule in the sortable sheet, `list/styles/sortable`, that `mx-list` doesn't adopt (`RF-129`).
  2. An item that isn't in a drag keeps its `user-select`, so a press that moves less than the threshold still selects text (row 3).
  3. drag doesn't change, and neither does `drag:DRI-11`.
- **Rows,** `browser`, in each engine, by real mouse input: the implementer's three, with rows 1 and 2 for each of the three item kinds. Also **row 4:** the probe's case, in which the held pointer leaves the list over page text, with the selection read during the drag and after the drop. **Witnesses,** in WebKit: without the rule, rows 1, 2 and 4 fail. With the rule on every item, not only in a drag, row 3 fails. If a row reads differently in an engine, or for an item kind, the implementer stops and returns it.
- **Not read:** Firefox, beyond CI. Safari. An item with a handle, whose handle is inside the item and so takes the rule with it. A link item's native drag, which `draggable="false"` already concerns (`drag:DRI-19`).
- **Also owed:** sizes by `just size`, in which `list/sortable-list` grows by a few bytes. The list's JSDoc and `list.mdx` don't change, because they promise nothing about selection. A feature proof follows. **Size:** _small_.

**Dated 2026-11-26 by the architect: the button item's rows stay without a witness, and row 3 stays on `mx-list-item`,** requested by the coordinator, on the implementer's return at `9ff1737ab`. The rule is `::slotted(:state(drag)) { -webkit-user-select: none; user-select: none; }`, with WebKit's prefix. With it, the 8 rows pass in WebKit and Chromium. In WebKit, without the rule, rows 1 and 2 fail for `mx-list-item` and `mx-list-link-item`, and row 4 fails too. **`mx-list-button-item` passes rows 1 and 2 without the rule.** With the rule on every item, row 3 fails in both engines.

- **Rows 1 and 2 stay for `mx-list-button-item`,** as rows without a witness. Property 1 is the list's for every kind, and this kind holds it today because of WebKit: a drag that starts on a `<button>` doesn't extend the press's selection. The rows cost nothing, and they fail if a change of the item's control or of the engine brings the highlight back. The record says that they have no witness.
- **Row 3 stays on `mx-list-item` alone.** Property 2 says that the list writes no `user-select` on an item outside a drag. The rule doesn't depend on the item's kind, and the witness, the rule on every item, fails row 3. What a short press selects in a button or a link is the engine's own behavior: a button item's press selects `I` in WebKit and nothing in Chromium, and a link item's press selects nothing in either. A row of those kinds would read the engine, not the list.
- **Not read, and not owed:** why a link item's press selects nothing in WebKit, while its drag extends a selection.

**Dated 2026-11-26 by the implementer: the repair is implemented on `material-x/drag-selection-1`,** from `42db3f321`. The rule is in `packages/material-x/src/list/styles/sortable/main.styles.css`, and the build prints both properties. The eight rows are in `packages/material-x/tests/list/sortable-list.browser.test.ts`, describe _"mx-sortable-list text selection"_. A comment above `mx-list-button-item`'s rows 1 and 2 says that they have no witness.

#### RF-152 — `parseMs` reads a duration in milliseconds as seconds

Tier C, **closed 2026-11-26** by #315, on `material-x/parse-ms-1`, at its merge (the last note). Before closure: open, ready. Pre-existing. Registered on 2026-11-26 by the architect, on `material-x/sortable-displacement-1`, from the implementer's point 4 in `RD-60`'s unit, relayed by the coordinator. `RF-151` is the entry before this one. Read at `5448c4fd6`.

- **What happens:** `parseMs` in `packages/material-x/src/core/utils/fns.ts` returns `parseFloat(value) * 1000`, whatever the value's unit, so `250ms` reads as 250,000 ms. It has done so since `b140ce683`. It reads the ripple's two durations, the sortable list's landing since `RF-109` (#199), and the list's layout animation since `RD-60`.
- **Why the values are right today:** each value that reaches it is a tproc motion token, which tproc writes in milliseconds, such as `500ms`. lightningcss, which every material-x sheet passes through, prints a time of 100 ms or more in seconds, minified or not, and keeps `99ms` and `50ms` as they are ([reading](sortable-displacement-1/checks/lightningcss-time.txt), [probe](sortable-displacement-1/probes/lightningcss-time.mjs)). tproc's shortest motion duration is 150 ms. The properties are private, and no public property feeds them.
- **Why it is a problem:** the function is right because of a printer's choice that nothing records. A token under 100 ms, or a value that doesn't pass through lightningcss, gives a duration 1,000 times too long, with no error.
- **Tier C:** no consumer reads a wrong duration, and no row relies on it.
- **Required property:** `parseMs` returns milliseconds for a `<time>` in either unit: `0.25s` and `250ms` both give 250. It throws on a value that has no number, as today. **Witness:** a row that gives a private duration in `ms` fails at `5448c4fd6`.
- **Plan needed:** no. **Size:** _small_.

**Dated 2026-11-26 by the implementer: the repair is implemented on `material-x/parse-ms-1`,** from `d6f6cf60b`, in Chromium (`RD-62`). `parseMs` scales a value by 1,000 unless it ends in `ms`, and it still throws a `CSSVariableError` on a value with no number.

- **Rows:** `packages/material-x/tests/core/utils/fns.browser.test.ts` reads `0.25s`, `250ms`, `0s`, `0ms`, `1.5s` and `99ms`, and throws on `''`, `auto` and `ms`. The neighbors' timing row in `tests/list/sortable-list.browser.test.ts` now runs with `0.25s` and with `250ms`.
- **Witness:** at `d6f6cf60b`, the `250ms` and `99ms` rows of `parseMs` fail (250000 and 99000), and so does the neighbors' `250ms` row (duration 250000). The other rows pass.
- **Consumers don't change:** each value of the four properties in material-x's compiled sheets is in seconds: the ripple's `0.15s` and `0.5s`, the landing's `0.65s` and the layout animation's `0.5s` ([reading](parse-ms-1/checks/durations.txt)). Before and after the repair, `parseMs` gives the same milliseconds for each of them.
- **Checks:** material-x's browser project passes in Chromium (1425 rows). Lint and typecheck are clean.

**Dated 2026-11-26 by the architect, on `material-x/parse-ms-1`: the required property covers a unit in capitals, so the implementer owes a check that ignores the unit's case.** Requested by the coordinator, on `reviewer-1` of the [feature proof](reviews/parse-ms-1/feature-proof-claude.md#reviewer-1-a-time-with-its-unit-in-capitals-still-reads-1000-times-too-long) of `4fcc0a457`.

- **Ruling:** _"a `<time>` in either unit"_ names the CSS type, and [CSS Values 4](https://www.w3.org/TR/css-values-4/#dimensions) makes a unit identifier ASCII case-insensitive. So `250MS` and `250Ms` are `<time>`s in milliseconds, and each engine computes them as `0.25s` ([spellings](reviews/parse-ms-1/checks/spellings.txt)). `parseMs` owes 250 for each.
- **Why:** reading them as seconds would leave the defect that this entry registers: a value is right only because lightningcss prints units in lowercase, and nothing records that. The case of the unit isn't a defensive check against invalid usage, since the value is valid CSS. The cost is one case fold per read.

- **What the implementer owes:** `parseMs` reads the unit regardless of case. Rows in `tests/core/utils/fns.browser.test.ts` read `250MS` and `250Ms` as 250, `0.25S` as 250, and throw on `MS`. **Witness:** the `250MS` and `250Ms` rows fail at `4fcc0a457` (250000). `0.25S` and `MS` already pass there, so they fix the contract and don't witness the change. Nothing else in the entry changes.

Lint and typecheck are clean.

#### RF-153 — material-x's node tests build with a private-property list that may be stale

Tier B, **closed 2026-11-26** by #316 at `6588c7361` (the last note). Before closure: open, ready. Pre-existing. Registered on 2026-11-26 by the architect, on `material-x/sortable-displacement-1`, from observation 1 of #310's [feature proof](reviews/sortable-displacement-1/feature-proof-claude.md#observations), relayed by the coordinator. `RF-152` is the entry before this one. Read at `c2ea0dcbe`.

- **What happens:** the node project's global setup, `packages/material-x/tests/support/build-package.node.ts`, runs `tsdown` alone, which is `just build-lib`. Mangling reads `node_modules/.cache/css/css-private-props.json`, which only `just build-prepare` (`.scripts/css/collect-props.ts`) writes. In a tree whose sheets have a private property that the list lacks, the build fails with _"Property `--_layout-animation-duration` is not collected"_. Every file of the project then fails, as the proof saw in its slot before it ran `build-prepare`. A tree whose sheets changed without a new name builds with the old list's short names, which differ from what a fresh list gives.
- **Why it is a problem:** a local run of the node rows, which implementers and proofs make, can fail for a reason that isn't the code, and nothing in the error names `build-prepare`. Or the rows can read a build that `just build` and CI wouldn't make from the same tree. CI isn't affected, because it builds first.
- **Required property:** the build that the node project reads is made from a property list collected from the tree under test, so that a local run of the project gives the result that CI gives on the same tree. **Witness:** with a stale list, after a private property is added to a sheet, the project's rows pass, and they fail at `c2ea0dcbe`.
- **Not read:** whether `build-prepare`'s run time matters to the project's setup, and the other packages' node setups, whose builds don't mangle these names.
- **Plan needed:** no. **Size:** _small_.

A failure of either is provided as the build's failure, as before.

#### RF-154 — Storybook's manager rebuilds its URL with the theme that the URL had when it loaded

Tier C, **closed 2026-11-27** by #323, on `repo/storybook-theme-1`, at its merge (the last note). Before closure: open, ready. Pre-existing. Registered on 2026-11-26 by the architect, on `repo/register-observations-10`, from [#317](https://github.com/ausginer/material-x/issues/317), requested by the coordinator. `RF-153` is the highest `RF-` on any branch on `origin`, so this is the next free number. Read at `d6f6cf60b`, with Storybook 10.6.7, in Chromium, against `storybook dev` on that tree ([reading](register-observations-10/checks/theme.txt), [probe](register-observations-10/probes/theme-probe.ts.txt)).

- **The owner's words,** of 2026-11-26: _"При переключении страницы/перезагрузке тёмная тема слетает."_ ("On switching page or reloading, the dark theme is lost.") Later the same day, rechecked: _"Перепроверил #317, внезапно всё работает 🤔 Втф, утром не работало 100%"_ ("Rechecked #317, suddenly everything works. WTF, this morning it 100% didn't work"). And, relayed by the coordinator in English only: after he switched to light, a navigation kept `theme=dark` in the URL, and the other way round, and sometimes it works.
- **What happens:** the theme toggle in the toolbar switches the preview at once. What the next sidebar navigation shows depends on the URL that the manager loaded with, not on the toggle:
  - **Loaded without `theme=dark`:** toggled to dark, the next story opens light, and the URL says `theme=light`. A reload then stays light (reading, A2 to A4).
  - **Loaded with `theme=dark`:** navigation and reload keep dark (B1 to B3). Toggled back to light, the next story opens dark again (B4, B5).
  - So the owner's recheck and his first report are both right, if the recheck started from a URL that said `theme=dark`. Nothing that Storybook loads changed between them: the last commits to `.storybook/` and to the root manifest's Storybook versions are before 2026-11-25, and the repository has no Pages workflow.
- **The cause, by reading:** the theme lives only in the `theme` query parameter of the manager's URL. `.storybook/manager.tsx`'s toggle writes it with `window.history.replaceState` (`setUrlTheme`), and `.storybook/preview.ts` writes it again in its decorator on every story render (`setTopUrlTheme`). The manager's router doesn't observe `replaceState`. Storybook's manager builds each navigation's URL from the `customQueryParams` of its own state (`navigateWithQueryParams`, `buildNavigationUrl` in `storybook/dist/manager/globals-runtime.js`), which it reads from the router's location. So a navigation writes back the `theme` of the load, and the preview's decorator then applies that value and writes it again. The manager re-reads the URL into `customQueryParams` only when the router's location changes, and a reload reads it afresh, so a reload straight after a toggle keeps the toggle, and one after a navigation keeps the reverted value. The toolbar's `useAddonState` isn't reset by the navigation, so its icon can disagree with the preview's theme. The decorator's rewrite and the icon are inferred from the code. The probe reads only the theme and the URL. Mx Architect Explainer read the same cause in `storybook/dist/manager-api/index.js`, approved by the owner as input and relayed by the coordinator.
- **Why it is a problem:** a reader of the docs who chooses the dark theme loses it on the next page, and can't choose light again in a session that started dark. The behaviour depends on how the page was opened, so a report of it looks intermittent.
- **Tier C:** the docs site isn't in any package's exports, and no gate row reads the theme.
- **Required property:** the theme that the reader last chose in the toolbar, or with a docs page's toggle, is the theme of every story and docs page that a sidebar navigation or a reload opens, whatever the URL said at load, in each engine. The preview and the manager have one source for it. **Witness:** the probe, at the repair, reads dark at A3 and A4 and light at B5. At `d6f6cf60b` it reads light, light and dark.
- **The direction, for the unit that takes it:** keep the theme in state that the manager carries through its navigation and its URL. Not a second `replaceState`.
  - **Recommended: a Storybook global, `theme`,** from `globalTypes` and `initialGlobals`. The decorator reads it from the story's context, the toolbar sets it with `updateGlobals`, and the docs pages' `ThemeToggleLink` sets it through the channel. Storybook writes it as `globals=theme:…` and keeps it through navigation and reload, so both URL writers go, with `top.history` and its cross-origin `try`. `@storybook/addon-themes`, which the root manifest already declares, unused, at 10.6.7, keeps one such global. This is Mx Architect Explainer's proposal, and the architect's choice, because it gives the preview and the manager one source.
  - **The smaller alternative:** write the parameter through the manager's `api.applyQueryParams({ theme })`, which updates `customQueryParams`. The preview still writes its own copy, so it keeps two writers.
  - **Not checked:** whether a global reaches the docs pages through the repository's `DocsContainer`. The unit reads it first.
- **The owner's answer** to the direction, of 2026-11-26, relayed by the coordinator: _"давай попробуем, но, помнится, globals меня жестоко забуллил в своё время, так что может и не сработать 😅"_ ("Let's try it, but as I recall, globals gave me a really hard time back then, so it may not work.")
  - **So the unit tries the global first.** If a global doesn't hold where the required property needs it, on a docs page through `DocsContainer` or across a navigation or a reload, the unit stops and returns with the reading. The architect then rules on `applyQueryParams`, which is the fallback.
- **Not decided:** whether a new visit, without the parameter, opens with the last theme or with the system's. The property doesn't ask it.
- **Not read:** Firefox, WebKit, the deployed site, the docs pages' `ThemeToggleLink` after a navigation, the cause line by line in the router.
- **Plan needed:** no. **Size:** _small_.

**Dated 2026-11-27 by the implementer: the theme is a Storybook global, on `repo/storybook-theme-1`,** from `085be1e2b`, in Chromium (`RD-62`), against `storybook dev`. The global holds where the property needs it, so the owner's condition doesn't apply and `applyQueryParams` isn't used.

- **What changed:** `.storybook/preview.ts` declares the `theme` global with `initialGlobals` (`light`). The preview applies the globals that `GLOBALS_UPDATED` reports, because Storybook emits it for every story render, every docs render and every update. **Corrected 2026-11-27 by the implementer,** on `reviewer-2` and the architect's ruling below. This said: _"declares the `theme` global with `globalTypes` and `initialGlobals` (`light`). Its decorator applies the global from the story's context, and the preview also applies the globals that `SET_GLOBALS` and `GLOBALS_UPDATED` report, because a docs page runs no decorator of its own."_ No path that was read needs the decorator or `SET_GLOBALS`. The toolbar in `.storybook/manager.tsx` reads and sets it with `useGlobals`. `ThemeToggleLink` emits `UPDATE_GLOBALS`. Both `replaceState` writers, the read of `top.location` with its `try`, `THEME_EVENT` and the toolbar's addon state go. Storybook writes the global as `globals=theme:dark` and drops it for the initial value.
- **The docs pages, read first:** `DocsContainer` passes nothing of its own. A docs page follows the global through the channel's `GLOBALS_UPDATED`, which Storybook's channel also delivers to the emitting frame's listeners.
- **Witness** ([reading](storybook-theme-1/checks/theme.txt), [probe](storybook-theme-1/probes/theme-probe.ts.txt)): A3 and A4 read dark, and B5 reads light. The probe now reads `globals` from the URL, and B loads with `globals=theme:dark`. It adds C1 to C8 on docs pages: a docs page's toggle to dark holds through a sidebar navigation to another docs page, a reload and a story, and its toggle back to light holds through a navigation. The entry's probe, unchanged, reads dark at A3 and A4. Its B opens light, because nothing reads `theme=dark` now ([reading](storybook-theme-1/checks/theme-original.txt)).
- **Observation:** an old link with `?theme=dark` now opens light. The entry doesn't decide what a new visit opens with.
- **Checks:** lint and typecheck are clean. Not read: Firefox, WebKit, the deployed site.

**Ruled 2026-11-27 by the architect, on the two findings of #323's [feature proof](reviews/storybook-theme-1/feature-proof-claude.md) at `be4f7eee2`,** requested by the coordinator. Read on `repo/storybook-theme-1` at `4a2a80452`: the proof's readings and mutation summary, `.storybook/preview.ts`, `stories-reading.ts` with `BQ-21`, and Storybook 10.6.7's `dist/preview/runtime.js`. Both are remediation inside the unit, so nothing is the owner's, and nothing is minted.

- **`reviewer-1`: tier B, fixed on this branch.** `BQ-21` is implemented, and one of its properties is retaken on each change to box-quad's stories: _"Each story gets a screenshot in both themes in Chromium, retaken"_. So `stories-reading.ts` is a standing instrument, not a closed unit's record. At the head its `theme=dark` opens light in every engine, and `globals=theme:dark` opens dark in a standalone `iframe.html` ([reading](reviews/storybook-theme-1/checks/old-link.txt)). The implementer:
  - writes the story URL with `globals=theme:<theme>` (`storyUrl`, line 75);
  - makes `openStory` refuse a story whose `document.documentElement.dataset.theme` isn't the theme it asked for, naming the story and both themes. A later change to how the preview applies the theme then stops the run instead of writing light screenshots under dark names. **Witness:** with `theme=` restored, the run refuses the first dark story;
  - reruns the script on the built docs site, as `BQ-21` does. The four `*-dark.png` files are dark. Each screenshot that differs from the committed one is committed with the reason, and the light ones are expected not to differ, because #323 changes no style that box-quad's stories use. A dated note under `BQ-21` in box-quad's plan records the run and its output.
- **`reviewer-2`: tier C, fixed on this branch: `GLOBALS_UPDATED` is the one mechanism.** Storybook 10.6.7 emits it after preparing every story render and every docs render (`renderSelection`), and again on every `UPDATE_GLOBALS` (`onUpdateGlobals`). The mutations agree in the three engines: without the decorator, without `SET_GLOBALS`, or without both, no reading changes, and without `GLOBALS_UPDATED` the storyless page can't be switched to light. The decorator and the `SET_GLOBALS` listener are then a second and a third way to do the same thing, and no path that was read needs them. The implementer:
  - removes the decorator and the `SET_GLOBALS` listener, and `globalTypes`. A global is accepted from the URL when `initialGlobals` or `globalTypes` names it (`allowedGlobalNames`, `runtime.js` line 14333), so `initialGlobals` is enough, and `global-types-off` survives in the three engines. `initialGlobals` stays: it is what drops the global from the URL for light;
  - rewrites the listener's comment with its reason: Storybook reports the globals on this event for every story and docs render and for every update, and a docs page or a page without a story runs no decorator;
  - corrects the implementer's note above, where it gives the decorator and `SET_GLOBALS` a reason.
  - **Costs, accepted:** a fresh load straight into a story whose file fails to load shows Storybook's error in light, because only `SET_GLOBALS` comes before that error. Each other page in a dark session is dark. The theme now relies on one Storybook event, and no gate reads the theme, so a Storybook upgrade that stops emitting it on render would show as unthemed stories and docs pages. That is visible to a reader, and the theme probe is the reading to rerun.
  - **Witness:** the unit's theme probe and the proof's standalone drag loads read the same at the fix as at `4a2a80452`, in Chromium (`RD-62`). The proof's `only-globals-updated`, `only-globals-updated-drag` and `global-types-off` already read that in the three engines, and `globals-updated-off` stays the witness that the listener is needed.

**Dated 2026-11-27 by the implementer: both rulings are implemented, on `repo/storybook-theme-1`,** after `5a85ec385`, in Chromium (`RD-62`), requested by the coordinator.

- **`reviewer-1`:** box-quad's `stories-reading.ts` writes `globals=theme:<theme>`, and `openStory` refuses a story whose `data-theme` isn't the theme it asked for. Run on the built docs site, every reading is the committed one, and all eight screenshots are byte-equal to the committed ones, so none is committed again. The four `*-dark.png` files are dark. **Witness:** with `theme=` put back, the run stops at _"live-demo: the preview's theme is light, not dark"_, the first dark story.
